result.cluster: FluoroCap: the corpus, its pipeline and its audits

candidates.topic: Figure-mate region agreement with constraint decoding versus the level model alone (same corpus, same date, 2026-09-14)
candidates.statement_a: The card's evaluation table gives 88% figure-mate region agreement for the decoder and 52% for the model alone, with no pair count.
candidates.quote_a: figure mates agreeing on region (decoder) | 88% | panels of the same figure with the same caption levels; 52% for the model alone (partly induced by the shared caption)
candidates.statement_b: The audit of the same day gives 91.5% for the decoder on 519 pairs and 52.1% for the model alone on 468 pairs.
candidates.quote_b: Constraint decoding lifts caption-free region agreement from 52.1% to 91.5% ... 519 pairs for the decoder, 468 for the model run alone.
candidates.why_it_matters: The decoder's headline number is either 88% or 91.5% for the same quantity on the same date; a planner citing one page misquotes the other, and only the audit says how many pairs were counted.

candidates.topic: What the panels without a vertebra box are: detector misses or non-radiographs
candidates.statement_a: The audit reads the 71% of known panels without a box as mostly detector misses, because the modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set.
candidates.quote_a: Only 29% of known panels produced a vertebra box . The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
candidates.statement_b: The reality check scores nearly half the corpus as not an x-ray at all, and 35% of the level-labelled panels as not spine radiographs.
candidates.quote_b: 8,843 (49%) score as not an x-ray at all. In the released manifest of 17,486 rows, 9,036 sit below the 0.3 floor, 4,218 pass the default inclusion rules, and human_qc_status reads pending on every row. Of the 2,071 decoded panels that carry level labels, 732 (35%) are
candidates.why_it_matters: The two readings point to opposite fixes: detector recall work under the audit, corpus filtering under the reality check; a planner who read only the audit would retrain the detector on a corpus that is half non-radiographs.

candidates.topic: The 2,143-panel held-out set behind the 93% modality score: FluoroCap panels or film-manifest classes
candidates.statement_a: The audit presents the 93% modality score as measured on 2,143 held-out panels and applies it to FluoroCap's missing 71%.
candidates.quote_a: The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
candidates.statement_b: The reality check says the 2,143 / 800 held-out set is film-manifest classes, not FluoroCap panels, and that modality is unknown for 7,642 of 17,486 manifest rows.
candidates.quote_b: 93.1% modality head / 99.5% view head | | 2,143 / 800 held-out | | film-manifest classes | | not FluoroCap panels; modality is 'unknown' for 7,642 of 17,486 manifest rows
candidates.why_it_matters: The audit's inference about FluoroCap rests on a score measured on a different population; a planner would trust the modality filter on mined figures when it was never tested on them.

candidates.topic: Caption-held-out accuracy of the level model alone, and containment of its level set
candidates.statement_a: The audit (2026-09-14): the level model alone is right 38.3% of the time with the caption held back; containment 56.8% on n = 389.
candidates.quote_a: The level model alone is right 38.3% of the time on panels where the caption was held back. ... 56.8% caption-held-out containment, n = 389
candidates.statement_b: The reality check (2026-09-15): 37.9% on 169 panels; 57.1% containment, Jaccard 0.341, on 380 caption-free panels that are not a random hold-out.
candidates.quote_b: the level model alone is the weakest term in the decoder on real panels (37.9% on 169) ... 57.1% containment, Jaccard 0.341 | | 380 'caption-free' panels | | ... not a random hold-out
candidates.why_it_matters: The sample sizes and values drift between the two pages and the later one says the sample is not a random hold-out, so neither number is a generalisable accuracy; a planner quoting 38.3% or 56.8% from the audit would cite a figure the next day's page withdrew.

candidates.topic: Where every panel comes from: open-licence published figures only, or also surgical video frames
candidates.statement_a: The card asserts every panel is a figure published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository.
candidates.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
candidates.statement_b: The audit of the same day counts 479 surgical video frames in the corpus, mined from surgical video.
candidates.quote_b: The corpus is eleven thousand panel images mined from the literature and from surgical video. ... surgical video frames | | 479
candidates.why_it_matters: A licence tier or a Dataset B release decided from the card's provenance sentence would include video frames the card says do not exist; the card's statement does not describe the corpus the audit counted.

candidates.topic: Provenance of the corpus versus the closed-journal refetch and the Instagram harvest
candidates.statement_a: The card: every panel is an openly licensed published figure, nothing institutional was accessed.
candidates.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
candidates.statement_b: The access setup refetches about 600 closed-journal figures through the owner's institutional sign-in and harvests Instagram with a dedicated account against Meta's terms.
candidates.quote_b: The refetch touches only the closed-journal figures that already carry a matched caption (about 600), one request every three seconds per host ... Meta's terms prohibit automated collection. Accounts used for it get action-blocked, then disabled. Use a dedicated account
candidates.why_it_matters: The overnight report says the proxy session was used on 653 figures; a planner relying on the card would treat the whole corpus as redistributable when part of it came from closed journals and a platform whose terms forbid the collection.

candidates.topic: Rule for sources whose terms forbid automated collection
candidates.statement_a: The access setup plans to harvest Instagram despite Meta's prohibition, by using a dedicated account.
candidates.quote_a: Meta's terms prohibit automated collection. Accounts used for it get action-blocked, then disabled. Use a dedicated account
candidates.statement_b: The registry (2026-10-20) treats the YouTube copies as unpermitted until a request is answered, and the Honest 99 report says Radiopaedia and Eurorad are not scraped.
candidates.quote_b: the YouTube copies are unpermitted until a request is answered
candidates.why_it_matters: The cluster holds two rules at once: harvest around the terms, or hold the copies until permission comes; a planner needs to know which applies before scaling any platform route (the reality check lists scaling YouTube and Instagram under what to stop).

candidates.topic: Releasing FluoroCap (Dataset A and B licence tiers) versus the private-forever rule
candidates.statement_a: The card is a release card with licence tiers, Dataset A and Dataset B, commercial-training eligibility and an examples section.
candidates.quote_a: 10. Examples · Dataset A only (non-commercial or share-alike licences)
candidates.statement_b: The lab recipe (2026-09-27) lists FluoroCap as private forever, never in a public repository or on the website.
candidates.quote_b: Private forever | Level-identification code, FluoroCap, model weights, spinesurg-ct-nnunet, XRSpinoPelvic1K. Never in a public repository, never on the website. | the website shipped 121 MB of weights until 2026-09-14
candidates.why_it_matters: A planner working from the card would prepare a public release the later rule forbids; the card's licence tiers and Dataset A/B split only matter if a release is still intended.

candidates.topic: Whether FluoroCap may train the level model
candidates.statement_a: The audit forbids retraining on the corpus only without re-weighting, so retraining with re-weighting is allowed.
candidates.quote_a: this corpus must not be used to retrain the level model without re-weighting
candidates.statement_b: The reality check makes the mined figures and video an external test set only, never for the level head.
candidates.quote_b: Tier 4, the mined figures and video: an external test set only, after a two-reader read of a stratified sample ... never for the level head.
candidates.why_it_matters: The Honest 99 report of 2026-09-16 says training on the enlarged corpus was still running; a planner who followed the audit would put the corpus into the training bank that the reality check and the later directive exclude it from.

candidates.topic: FluoroCap crops still in the C-ArmLSpine fold banks despite the directive
candidates.statement_a: The handoff (2026-10-08) finds 2,100 FluoroCap crops per fold bank behind the fine-tuned naming numbers.
candidates.quote_a: The C-ArmLSpine fold models behind the fine-tuned naming numbers still train on 2,632 VinDr crops and 2,100 FluoroCap crops per fold bank, plus both NHANES copies ... That contradicts the directive that FluoroCap is out of every training set
candidates.statement_b: The registry (2026-10-20) records FluoroCap as out of training by directive D1, a test set at most.
candidates.quote_b: out of training by directive D1, a test set at most
candidates.why_it_matters: The registry states the rule as in force while the handoff twelve days earlier shows the banks violating it; a planner reading the registry would believe the fine-tuned numbers are clean of FluoroCap.

candidates.topic: The 99% selective-accuracy claim and its held-out status
candidates.statement_a: The Honest 99 report (2026-09-16) states the 99% selective accuracy is measured on held-out renders.
candidates.quote_a: Among the vertebrae it names, the model is right 99% of the time — and it names 35.7% of them. ... It is measured on held-out renders, which is stated wherever it appears
candidates.statement_b: The handoff (2026-10-08) rules the allspine v2 family leaked and the 99% selective-accuracy claim record only; the reality check already said every render evaluation overlaps training.
candidates.quote_b: allspine v2, v6 and v7, anchor_drr and vindrps are leaked families, and every number from them is record only, including the 99.02 % shortcut-free film number and the 99 % selective-accuracy claim
candidates.why_it_matters: The number the talk would lead with is, per the later record, measured on a leaked split; a planner reading only the Honest 99 page would present it as held out.

candidates.topic: How many panels were decoded and labelled before 2026-09-16 (the baseline the Honest 99 report compares against)
candidates.statement_a: The Honest 99 report says 5,789 panels decoded and 4,614 carrying a level 'yesterday morning'.
candidates.quote_a: 20,700 panels decoded and 11,377 carrying a level, against 5,789 and 4,614 yesterday morning.
candidates.statement_b: The audit of 2026-09-14 counts three thousand labelled panels, and the reality check of 2026-09-15 counts 3,294 panels decoded and 2,071 carrying level labels.
candidates.quote_b: The corpus is eleven thousand panel images mined from the literature and from surgical video. Three thousand of them carry machine-assigned vertebra labels.
candidates.why_it_matters: The growth the Honest 99 report claims is measured against a baseline no earlier page reports; a planner cannot reconcile the decoded counts across the three days.

candidates.topic: Whether any real panel carries an L6 or T13 label
candidates.statement_a: The Honest 99 anomaly table lists 338 panels for L6 and 254 for T13 among panels carrying a level.
candidates.statement_b: The reality check: no real panel is labelled L6 and no real-film crop exists; the 802 L6 crops come from at most 90 CT cases.
candidates.quote_b: L6 | 0 panels labelled; 0 real-film crops | 802 crops from at most 90 distinct cases (56 VerSe + 34 CTSP)
candidates.why_it_matters: Whether a real-film transitional test set exists decides the whole transitional-anatomy plan; one page says hundreds of panels, the previous day's says zero (the audit also says the labels were never assigned to a single real panel).

candidates.topic: Real L6 cases available for a transitional test
candidates.statement_a: The registry (2026-10-20) credits C-ArmLSpine with three real L6 cases.
candidates.quote_a: 3 real L6 cases
candidates.statement_b: The handoff (2026-10-08) counts zero verified real-frame transitional test persons against 35 needed.
candidates.quote_b: 0 verified real-frame transitional test persons against 35 needed
candidates.why_it_matters: A planner needs to know whether the three cases are verified; the registry's count and the handoff's zero are not reconciled.

candidates.topic: Images on disk after the refetch (figure panels, video, video-medium)
candidates.statement_a: The overnight report (2026-09-15, morning): 19,048 images on disk, 17,755 figure panels, 927 video, 366 medium-confidence video.
candidates.quote_a: Images on disk went from 11,349 to 19,048: 17,755 figure panels ..., 927 video panels and 366 medium-confidence video panels
candidates.statement_b: The reality check, later the same day: 19,581 (18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium), explicitly superseding 19,048.
candidates.quote_b: 19,581 (18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium) | | find on ~/FluoroCap; morning report's 19,048 superseded
candidates.why_it_matters: Both pages are canonical in the clustering; the counts differ and the reality check says which stands.

candidates.topic: Corpus size over time: 11,349 to 19,581 to 20,700 decoded to 29,500 panels
candidates.statement_a: The reality check (2026-09-15): 19,581 images on disk.
candidates.quote_a: 19,581 (18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium)
candidates.statement_b: The atlas (2026-10-17): 29,500 panels and a manifest of 21,603 rows; the Honest 99 report in between gives 20,700 decoded panels and 12,106 figures, and the OR ledger 29,484 panels.
candidates.quote_b: 29,500 panels (png); manifest 21,603 rows ...; frozen v0.1 A 2,531 / B 991 panels; YouTube 298,075 frames; 316 GB tree
candidates.why_it_matters: The canonical pages freeze the corpus at September counts; the October pages are the current ones, and a planner sizing reader time from a canonical page would be off by half.

candidates.topic: Closed-journal refetch: figures replaced and pixel gain
candidates.statement_a: Overnight report: 1,489 of 2,901 figures replaced, median 6.3x the pixels, round two still running.
candidates.quote_a: 1,489 of 2,901 figures replaced with the publisher's larger copy, median 6.3× the pixels; round two still running
candidates.statement_b: Reality check: 1,558 of 2,901 (53.7%), p50 gain 6.26x, superseding 1,489; the Honest 99 report then gives 2,059 replaced at 6.25x.
candidates.quote_b: 1,558 of 2,901 figures replaced (53.7%); pixel-area gain p50 6.26× ... round two still running; morning report's 1,489 superseded
candidates.why_it_matters: Three pages give three replacement counts for one running job; only the latest (Honest 99, 2,059) is a finished count.

candidates.quote_a: 927 video panels and 366 medium-confidence video panels
candidates.statement_b: 1,096 video panels and 366 video-medium.
candidates.quote_b: 18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium

candidates.topic: Which manifest version the pipeline produces on 2026-09-14
candidates.statement_a: The pipeline map draws the refresh orchestrator ending in manifest v0.3.

refresh orchestrator

candidates.topic: State of the all-spine v2 model on 2026-09-15
candidates.statement_a: The reality check (snapshot 06:55 to 07:15): the v2 weights were destroyed and the retrain job 40285209 is pending.
candidates.quote_a: the level model alone is the weakest term in the decoder on real panels (37.9% on 169), and the v2 model exists only as a validation JSON from weights that were destroyed ... weights destroyed by the chain's link step; retrain 40285209 pending at read time
candidates.statement_b: The overnight report's 08:30 update: the retrain resubmitted 05:47 registered a model at 08:13 and scores 64.2% on 800 held-out renders.
candidates.quote_b: All-spine v2 retrain (resubmitted 05:47): model registered 08:13; diagnostic and transitional test run held out 08:13 ... over 800 held-out renders it scores 64.2% ... That is the honest render number.
candidates.why_it_matters: The reality check is the clustering's successor page yet the overnight report's update postdates it on this item; a planner would wrongly think no v2 model exists.

candidates.topic: Job ids of the CUT translator v2 run

candidates.topic: Share of known panels with a vertebra box
candidates.statement_a: 29% of known panels produced a vertebra box.
candidates.quote_a: Only 29% of known panels produced a vertebra box .

candidates.topic: Design of the reference standard: two blind readers with adjudication, or one reader
candidates.statement_a: The card specifies two readers blind to each other and to the proposal, with a third adjudicating.
candidates.quote_a: The protocol specifies two readers blind to each other and to the proposal, adjudication of disagreements by a third

candidates.topic: How many panels must be read to turn agreement into accuracy

candidates.topic: Sample size of the level verification bench against the stated requirement

canonical_check.why: The reality check (2026-09-15) re-measures every quantity the audit (2026-09-14) reports, on the refetched corpus of 19,581 images instead of 11,349, and says measurements outrank the morning report; its box rate (17.3% vs 29%), caption-held-out numbers (37.9%/57.1% vs 38.3%/56.8%), modality reading (49% not an x-ray vs detector miss) and Castellvi strata replace the audit's. The audit keeps content the reality check does not repeat (per-level recall, hardware constraints, renderer fixes, the 400-panel read plan), so it is superseded for its numbers, not deleted as a source.

The reality check explicitly supersedes the overnight report's counts (19,048 images, 1,489 refetched, 927 video panels) and says measurements outrank the morning report, so the overnight report is canonical only for what the reality check does not cover; but its 08:30 update postdates the reality check's 06:55 to 07:15 snapshot on the v2 model (registered 08:13, 64.2% on 800 renders) and on the CUT v2 job ids, so on those two items the overnight report is the later record. A superseded relation from overnight-report to reality-check, with the v2 items excepted, fits the records better than two canonical pages.

The card is a frozen 2026-09-14 09:43 view (10,281 rows, dataset 0.2) whose counts, figure-mate number (88%) and provenance sentence are contradicted the same day by the audit and superseded by the reality check (17,486 rows) and the atlas (21,603 rows, 29,500 panels); its licence tiers and release framing conflict with the later private-forever rule. It stays canonical for the licence tiers, inclusion and exclusion rules and the reader protocol, not for counts or release intent.

No later page redraws the pipeline, so the map remains the one description of the routes; its counts (197k frames, manifest v0.3) and its network and serving invariants are dated or contradicted (the access setup's grid plan, the lab recipe's 121 MB of shipped weights, the handoff's anchor_drr leak), so a reader takes its structure and not its numbers.

result.unsourced_summary: The dataset card and the pipeline map both assert that the manifest regenerates byte-identical from the same inputs and that an unbroken SHA-256 chain runs from original figure to weights, naming no command, run or checksum file. The map asserts that the grid's outbound IP is captcha-throttled by PMC while WSL is not, and the access setup asserts that publishers authenticate by IP from the university's address space; neither cites a probe, and the overnight report shows the refetch ran through the proxy session instead. The access setup asserts that video frames are the only 1080 px native source and that Instagram serves posts at 1080 px wide, with no measurement; the reality check says the YouTube panels came capped at 720p. The map's anchor panel asserts that an author's printed label is the strongest anchor there is, with no accuracy measured for printed labels, while the reality check says the caption's label was mostly assigned by counting on a limited field. The atlas and the registry both state that 72.8 percent of the 29,500 panels are reproductions with no pixel residual, naming no duplicate-detection run or threshold. The card's 88% figure-mate number carries no pair count. Lift Before Label asserts the renderer is already at the DeepDRR/SyntheX level with no test, and its own adversarial pass never ran. The adjudication bench asserts that the reader's single read is the only ground truth the panel will ever have, and the level verification bench assumes a whole-run-correct panel is the common case; neither assumption is measured, and the card's protocol promises two blind readers with a third adjudicating. The reality check's claims that 'Castellvi I is two thirds of transitional anatomy' and that registration-derived labels are biased are stated without a source in the records.
result.stale_summary: All six primary pages are snapshots of 14 to 15 September 2026 with running work inside them: the card says dataset version 0.2 with 0.3 in progress and reader labels pending for every panel; the pipeline map draws manifest v0.3 and 197k YouTube frames; the access setup says the PMC refetch is running now and worries about a library note of 30 June 2026; the overnight report says round two of the refetch is still running, the FluoroGen array was cancelled at 05:50, the CUT v2 is queued as jobs 40285316/7 and the v2 retrain registered at 08:13; the reality check, read between 06:55 and 07:15, says the v2 weights were destroyed and retrain 40285209 is pending, lists CUT jobs 40285274 and 40285275 as queued, and lays out a 90-day and 12-month plan from 15 September. The Honest 99 report of 16 September says training on the enlarged corpus, the backbone comparison and the render-physics test were still running. Later pages date them: the atlas of 2026-10-17 shows human_qc_status pending on all 21,603 rows and the two benches show 0 of 0 verified as of 2026-10-22, so the card's 'reader labels: none yet' still holds five weeks on; the handoff of 2026-10-08 says 14 cine sources, SX-Stitch and Balgrist requests are drafted and none sent, 0 verified real-frame transitional persons against 35 needed, and the registry of 2026-10-20 still calls VinDr's determination pending although the atlas three days earlier says HPR 2026-330 covers it (notice 2026-09-29) and the YouTube copies unpermitted until a request is answered. The lab recipe of 2026-09-27 says the website shipped weights until 2026-09-14. The CNS talk window (31 October to 4 November 2026) and the Radiopaedia USD 250 fee in the records are unconfirmed as of the records' dates.
result.notes: Quotes for the primary pages, the Honest 99 report, the handoff, the lab recipe, Lift Before Label, the level context ladder, the OR ledger and the three benches were checked against the plain texts; the extracted texts of fluoroscopy-data-atlas and schwingnet-data-registry truncate their embedded JSON and returned no hits for their key numbers, so those two artifacts are quoted from their inventory records only. Two of the readers' quotes named the university's network range, for which an editor's words now stand; no e-mail address, phone number or home address appears, and people are named by role (the owner, the reader). The FluoroGen 12,896 versus synth_rare 12,929 pair may be two different objects; it is listed because no page says so. The overnight report's 08:30 update postdating the reality check's snapshot is why the clustering's two canonical pages disagree on the v2 model state. Several secondary artifacts (Honest 99, handoff, registry, atlas) carry the later word on the corpus and the directive, so a reader of the canonical set alone would miss the private-forever rule, the leaked-family ruling and the October counts.

canonical_check.why: The handoff (3 Sep) records the film corpora as 77 BUU files, 0 CSXA images and IEEE, AASCE and BUU behind forms; the manifest (8 Oct) records the same corpora on disk at full size (CSXA 4,963 films; BUU 3,600 patients, 7,200 films; NHANES 17,073 and 543; VinDr 10,466; AASCE 609; Mendeley 714; IEEE 236; Spinal-AI 20,000), and the any-view plan says in its own words that the 3 Sep handoff had 77 BUU files while it reports BUU as held with 3,600 people. The manifest does not cite the handoff and does not carry its rules (the 208 Honduran films as the only cross-site test set, IEEE never for training, patient-disjoint splits, VinDr as restricted rather than credentialed), and the registry later excludes Mendeley outright, so the later page supersedes the holdings but not the lineage decisions; those survive only on the handoff, the board and the decisions page.

result.unsourced_summary: The September pages (the X-ray handoff and the vertebra-detector field report) assert that CSXA is the largest annotated lateral set in existence, that CM Spine is the only public intraoperative source, and that Google Drive caps folder downloads at about 50 files, none with a survey or a citation; the board and the decisions page, which copy each other, assert that no published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model, that the published state of the art on radiographs is AUC 0.84 at 62.3 % prevalence without naming the study, and that 4.0 % is the population LSTV rate, which the protocol draft puts at 15.3 % and research directions at 9 to 18 %. The 8 October trio (the handoff, the literature-state and research directions) share the statements that every planning value assumed 95 to 99 % with no measurement behind it, that 97.6 % cannot be exceeded at any reachable n, and that no radiologist has read any acquired CT, with the power figures 35, 22 and 19 and the accuracy pair 97.4 % and 74.8 % repeated without run ids or the calculation. The manifest, the registry and the FluoroCap card repeat that no patient was imaged for FluoroCap as the ethics basis with no determination cited. The atlas calls SX-Stitch the only published collection of overlapping intraoperative C-arm frames while the registry calls the Bern runs the only overlapping travelling frames found and the C-ArmLSpine sweeps the only confirmed consecutive sequences with a paired volume. Research directions states that Castellvi type I is 68 % of all LSTV with no reference. Licence statements for BUU (an EULA forbidding redistribution, on the manifest and research directions) stand beside the registry's own line that the licence is unread by the owner.
result.stale_summary: Every primary page is dated and overtaken: the X-ray handoff's grid state was verified 3 September 2026 (77 BUU files, no CSXA, IEEE behind a subscription, PhysioNet DUA 1.5.0, CSXA V3.0); the manifest is as of 7 October with batch B00 cut over and its finalize pending, B13 awaiting the owner's decision, the home walk still running, live routes untested and six licence conflicts (CTPelvic1K, VerSe, DeepFluoro, Geneva hip, Ljubljana, SpineSAC) marked unknown; the literature-state of 8 October says it is being cross-referenced and that no drafted request is recorded as sent; the atlas is as of 17 October with every request line reading Sent: not recorded and the Radiopaedia fee unconfirmed that day; the registry was rendered 20 October with its sample-level counts empty until a grid job runs, case39 with no export yet, LUMOS never fetched, RSNA 2022 never unpacked, ten VerSe series never downloaded, BUU's licence unread, VinDr's own determination pending, Balgrist and SX-Stitch requests drafted and never sent, and no gated CT agreement signed. The grid pipeline of 21 October then records 26 requests sent and 5 granted, a signed and paid Radiopaedia licence awaiting countersignature, VinDr-PCXR access granted on 21 October, an RSNA RATIC download link that expires 2026-10-28 02:38 UTC, 15 recipes still marked to confirm, no shard built and no job run, on a schedule running 23 October to 2 November with the provisional filing on 30 October and the CNS talk on 2 November. The secondary pages carry their own dates: the FluoroCap card's manifest was generated 2026-09-14 with reader labels pending and version 0.3 in progress; the board is dated 11 September with IRB files still public (the decisions page records the purge done); the lab recipe says the public mirror is still v10 on 2026-09-27; the 8 October handoff says the provisional filing is not recorded and the migration in progress; research directions says nothing ran on the grid and 33 were graded today; the any-view plan says the census job goes to the grid next and the IPCAI 2025 set is not yet held; the retrospective protocol is Date Submitted: Draft with an AIDaS deadline of 16 October 2026 already past and a target of January 2027; the eProtocol draft is dated 15 September with its 40,000-study cohort unconfirmed; and the COBRA embargoed cases are released on 2032-03-01.
result.notes: The plain-text extracts of the registry and the atlas truncate their embedded arrays after the first entry, so the registry's 60 records were read from the page's own JSON (const DATA in /home/user/SchwingNet/artifacts/schwingnet-data-registry/index.html) and the atlas's 217 entries from window.ATLAS in /home/user/SchwingNet/artifacts/fluoroscopy-data-atlas/index.html, extracted with a script run under python3 -I into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1b2f17bd-1fd4-5865-b98a-4797cc8ea3ad/scratchpad/helper/cluster_ds/registry.json and atlas.json; the quoted registry and atlas lines were verified there, the other artifacts' quotes come from their inventory records. The atlas entries confirmed the 150 Elekta exports, the SX-Stitch 'only published collection' line, DysphagiaBank at 87 files and 19 GB held, SpineSAC at 5,492 files with five or six C-arms, and the Bournemouth lumbar set as the only confirmed lumbar cine (a request source, so not in conflict with the atlas's 'found nowhere public' for lateral lumbar flexion-extension). Secondary pages dated 11 to 27 September (the board, decisions, lab recipe, field report, X-ray handoff, FluoroCap card, protocol drafts) are earlier than every primary page and most of their disagreements with the October pages are superseded holdings rather than live contradictions; they are listed where the later page does not say it replaces them. No e-mail address, phone number or home address was reproduced; people are named by role (the owner, the labellers, the corresponding authors, one neurosurgeon).

canonical_check.why: The decisions artifact carries the board's decisions, corpus table and licensing sentences forward verbatim and closes the board's open action: the board asks the owner to say go on the IRB-file purge, the decisions artifact records the purge done with git-filter-repo and verified. The decisions artifact also moves numbers the board gives (retraining target ~13,500 to ~34,000, Spinal-AI2024 from do-not-download to revisit), which is what superseding looks like, though the board is dated 2026-09-11 and the decisions artifact is undated.

result.unsourced_summary: The cluster asserts a set of field-level claims with no paper, run id or search behind them, and several are copied between artifacts. The board and decisions artifacts both state that no published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model and that the published LSTV state of the art is AUC 0.84 at 62.3% prevalence; only research-directions later names the second as Kwak 2025. The field report and the X-ray data handoff both call CSXA the largest annotated lateral set in existence and CM Spine the only public intraoperative source, while other artifacts treat DeepFluoro and C-ArmLSpine as real intraoperative sources. Counting-from-the-sacrum says published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96-0.98 and that a 28-point sim-to-real tax matches the field, while ninety-three-pixels says no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published and the 71.67% has no peer. The naming note and counting-levels repeat that half of surveyed neurosurgeons report a wrong-level event, 69.6%/97.6% surgeon accuracies, 52 minutes and 183 mGy per event, and 1 in 830 incidence; only the AIDaS proposal and research-directions attach names (Mody 2008, Manbachi 2018, Siminski 2023, Furuya 2026). Counting-against-two-anchors gives a 2% sixth-lumbar prior and a 'documented failure mode' with no document, and the rib audit calls counting from C2 the only definitive method. The decisions artifact gives a ResNet50 source-dataset F1 of 86.6% with no record. The any-view plan's 'lateral naming is at the ceiling' is graded Inferred with no second real device measured, and counting-levels asserts cadaver work needs no IRB while the proposal says the determination covers public de-identified data only.
result.stale_summary: The field report (undated, earliest) says the level head is not started, the ignore mask is unused, BUU holds 77 files and CSXA is blocked; the X-ray data handoff's grid state is 'verified 3 Sep 2026' with 800 BUU images never ingested and 0 CSXA on disk. The board (2026-09-11) waits on the owner for the IRB-file purge and is normalising ~22,000 radiographs; the decisions artifact records the purge done, lists Spinal-AI2024 as 'revisit' and a GitHub support ticket open. The ladder (2026-09-13) has jobs 40215523/40215525 running and the VinDr lumbar pipeline in progress; the naming note (2026-09-18) has the 376-patient transitional CV and the Klinwichit training running; counting-from-the-sacrum (2026-09-22) has an A/B and the id-is-a-person audit running and a fleet detector training; the OR ledger (2026-09-22) lists several jobs running, a re-score pending and no device fitted beyond the Cios Fusion; ninety-three-pixels (2026-09-21) has 8 GPU jobs and a decision on the table; what-is-left says the band test is 'being measured right now'. The handoff (2026-10-08) records the disclosure submitted 2026-09-25 with the provisional not recorded, the CNS talk 31 Oct-4 Nov, the Ceph migration and dataset letters not sent; research-directions (2026-10-08) says nothing ran on the grid and letters are not sent. The any-view plan (2026-10-21) has the census job built (PR #76) and going to the grid next, IPCAI 2025 'not yet', and is marked confidential before the provisional and 'before the talk'. The AIDaS proposal (due 2026-10-16, now past) carries [to confirm] placeholders, pending refiner and Fourier arms and a $20,000 request for 2027. The rib audit's v5 is a local tree with nothing pushed and sacral tests next; the two-anchors arms are proposed and not run; the pipeline map's versions are as of its 2026-09-14 commit.
result.notes: All 18 records were read whole and every quantity listed was checked against the plain text under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1b2f17bd-1fd4-5865-b98a-4797cc8ea3ad/scratchpad/text/SchwingNet/. The cluster spans five detector generations (958 images, 4,327, 11,007, 12,709 films, and render-only arms) and several C-ArmLSpine runs (120/141/148/149 cases), and most numeric disagreements are different runs reported as one fact rather than errors; the task was to list them, not to settle them. Items flagged with a caveat: the Ljubljana entries may be two distinct sets; the two patch sizes may belong to two networks; 90% vs 93.9% variance explained may be two quantities. The handoff's 'VinDr-SpineXR (0 of 10,466)' means not in the level bank, not a holding count, and its '2,293 DeepFluoro vendor frames' are the unused vendor frames, distinct from the 366. A file fluorocap-reality-check-czudvb.txt appeared in a grep but is not a member of this cluster and was not used. No e-mail, phone or address was reproduced; people are named by role (the owner, the radiologist, readers).

result.unsourced_summary: The cluster asserts a number of things with no source in any record. The clinical-need lines in Naming Vertebrae Without CT and Vertebral Levels Without CT (half of surveyed neurosurgeons report a wrong-level operation; 15 of 100 consecutive discectomies; 179 fiducial placements over 38 months at 52 minutes and 183 mGy) carry no citation in either page. Counting from the Sacrum states that published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96 to 0.98 and that the best published registration-free naming is 73.3% importing identity from a preoperative radiograph, with no paper named, and declares the naming problem solved to a standard nobody has published; Ninety-three Pixels says no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published and that the 71.67% has no peer, and that LevelCheck's 100% imports identity from the patient's own CT; Research Directions says no lumbosacral 3-D classifier exists at all. The Castellvi type I share (about two thirds in the Honest 99% page, 68% in Research Directions) and the sixth-lumbar prevalence of roughly 2% with a 97%-correct four-lumbar prior (Counting Against Two Anchors) are stated without sources, and the handoff itself says every planning value assumed 95 to 99% that no measurement supports. The handoff and the state-of-the-literature record both say the 97.6% comparator cannot be exceeded at any reachable n, without the calculation, and one calls it a LevelCheck figure and the other a reader figure. The OR-readiness ledger asserts that surgeons centre the field the same way every time and that FluoroCap's article list has no DeepFluoro, C-ArmLSpine, COBRA or Geneva paper, neither shown. The Honest 99% page says every number comes from a named file on the grid but names none, and the overnight report says three independent checks were run without naming them; the lab recipe tallies that 0 of 79 manifest keys begin with a job id. The level bench calls model-decided panels the common case with no count behind it. The REFORMS checklist states the grid's bash 4.2 and Python 3.6 and that a DOI cannot be withdrawn, both unsupported. The LSTV bench's modality and family guesses are machine guesses whose method is not stated.
result.stale_summary: As of 2026-10-22 the three benches (SchwingNet/level-verification-bench-mkjxsy, undated; SchwingNet/lstv-verification-bench-6m2qhr, 15 September 2026, pass one; SchwingNet/fluorocap-adjudication-bench-rnsyir, batch b1 from decode_v2_v2.jsonl) all show zero verdicts, and the October 8 records (Research Directions, the state of the literature, the handoff) say the verified real-frame transitional test count is zero. The FluoroCap chain is a sequence of same-week snapshots: the corpus audit (2026-09-14, 11,349 images, no human read), the dataset card (generated 2026-09-14 09:43, v0.1 frozen, v0.3 in progress, reader labels pending for every panel), the overnight report (2026-09-15, updated 08:30, MORNING_REPORT.md to be written, CUT v2 jobs queued), the reality check (2026-09-15 06:55 to 07:35, v2 retrain 40285209 pending, translator jobs queued, reading_set_b1 and reading_v2 built unread, 4,218 empty reader rows, a 90-day and 12-month plan) and the Honest 99% page (2026-09-16, counts against yesterday morning, ordinal-loss arm running, benches awaiting the owner), whose headline the October handoff marks record only. The narrative pages of 2026-09-18 (Naming, Vertebral Levels) have a 376-case CV running, a sacrum detector being built, a tolerant rule in testing and are themselves a post-leak rewrite that the later 92-of-97 audit overtakes. Ninety-three Pixels (2026-09-21) has eight GPU jobs running and a re-render decision left to the owner; the OR-readiness ledger (2026-09-22, re-scored 06:50) has ws_mixed 40411495 running, device fits in progress, the clean DeepFluoro retrain 40411934, a crop re-score pending and the styled corpus queued; Counting from the Sacrum (2026-09-22) has row (d) rendering, an A/B pending on a sampler implemented but not adopted, the fleet detector training on 18,906 frames and the CTSP1K id-is-person audit running, and the handoff says nothing after 2026-09-27 changed the banks. The feasibility study's deep-learning comparator is from October 2025. The lab recipe (2026-09-27) records the public mirror still at v10 and a pelvis DECISION.json never produced; the REFORMS checklist (2026-10-03) says none of its 32 gates exists. The October 8 records leave the dataset-request letters drafted and none sent, CHK-6 and CHK-7 never run, the leak check failing on a stale Geneva fixture, the provisional not recorded as filed against the 30 October deadline, and CNS on 31 October to 4 November 2026. Counting Against Two Anchors is an undated spec whose five arms are not run.
result.notes: The clustering gave no superseded or duplicate relations, so canonical_check is empty; the records themselves imply several the clustering omitted: the reality check (2026-09-15) explicitly supersedes the overnight report's image count (19,581 over 19,048); the OR-readiness ledger's 06:50 re-score supersedes its own 06:10 recall figure; Naming Vertebrae Without CT and Vertebral Levels Without CT are two tellings of one 2026-09-18 experiment with shared tables and the same confidentiality line, and the second says an earlier version was superseded after the leak audit; the handoff and Research Directions (2026-10-08) retire the Honest 99% page's headline as record only; Research Directions, the state of the literature and the handoff are one account's one-day audit repeated three times. All quotes are drawn from the inventory records; the plain-text files were not needed. Two number collisions are worth a warning rather than a candidate: 35.7% is both the v1 level model's accuracy on CT renders (audit, reality check) and the coverage at which the Honest 99% page reaches 99%, and 67.4% is both the majority-vote baseline that the sweep lifts to 91.8% and the L6 baseline that 83 real images lift to 73.5%. Several contradictions may be different scoring sets rather than errors (DeepFluoro seed spread, C2 on real, the 8,422-vertebra level-as-class row, count-alone 97.0 vs 99.96), and the why_it_matters says so where the quote does not fix the set. People are named by role (the owner, first and second account); literature authors are cited as the records cite them. canonical_check.why: Both are WSU eProtocol drafts of 'Protocol 1' for the retrospective fluoroscopy collection, mirroring IRB-21-10-4123. The retrospective protocol is the later text: it cites the 2 September 2026 determination 2026_269, the 16 October 2026 AIDaS deadline and a January 2027 start, where the other is dated 15 September 2026 and says 'Unfunded / departmental'. Neither record could confirm the order from its own text, but the dates and the AIDaS grant's 'builds-on' relation settle it. Caveat: the later draft is a redesign rather than a revision: Expedited 5 instead of Exempt 4, one surgeon's 2021-2026 cases instead of 40,000 studies from 2006, detector recall from operative-note truth instead of CT-registered labels, and the fracture-detection and registry-linkage aims, the 6,000-vertebrae stratified target and the 'Protocol 2 submitted alongside' line are dropped, not carried. The two also come from different accounts. So 'superseded' holds for the submission, but the older draft's aims are abandoned, and downstream notes (lift-before-label) still expect its registered frames.

result.unsourced_summary: The cluster's business case is held up by figures no artifact sources. The proposal (counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy), the seed grant (aidas-seed-grant-proposal) and the protocol (retrospective-fluoroscopy-protocol) all say every radiation-safety prerequisite takes fifteen business days, with no WSU page cited. The proposal and the grant assume the DMC PACS holds every saved fluoroscopic series of one surgeon's spine cases for 2021-2026 with operative notes and post-operative imaging for truth, while the older eProtocol draft and the fluorocap note cite another centre where half the cases were off PACS and the protocol's frames-per-case waits on a 20-case pilot. The proposal says cadaver work needs no IRB, the grant leaves phantom IACUC/RSC open, and the cadaver fee ($1,000-3,000) and the GPU, Jetson, grabber and phantom prices are list estimates with no quotes. The ten operating-room minutes saved per case (proposal) rest on two small non-randomised thoracic series that the visual abstract itself calls the weakest input, inflated by an unexplained 1.35 to 2026 dollars. The navigation comparison in the abstract, the grant and the protocol states that no study shows navigation reduces wrong-level surgery and that no verified capital cost exists, and the abstract's $1.5M over seven years plus 10% service is declared an assumption. Joint Commission 2024 (127, 9, 7, 36%) and NHS England (185) are cited by organisation name only in the grant, the protocol and the abstract; the proposal's registry figures carry no inline citation at all. The protocol's reason for Expedited 5, that research supporting an FDA submission cannot be exempt, and its line that the WSU form limits review to Exempt 2 and 3, cite no regulation; its sentence that synthetic fluoroscopy is tuned to one C-arm and one population is an inference from DeepFluoro alone; its expectation that a full count is possible on only a minority of archived cases is marked to confirm. The older draft's statements that no public intraoperative fluoroscopy with level labels exists (contradicted by the atlas) and that most spine-surgery patients have a pre- or post-operative CT have no source. Among the secondary notes, vertebral-levels-without-ct gives every literature figure without a citation and says 'fixing it took naming from 67% to 92%' with no run named, counting-from-the-sacrum says the 28-point sim-to-real tax 'matches what the field reports elsewhere almost exactly' without the field's numbers, and the OR-readiness ledger's 97% counting-grade threshold is a chosen line, not a derived one.
result.stale_summary: The proposal (counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy, September 2026) says 'Start this week' on the WSU C-arm and takes every synthetic number from the runs of 21 September 2026; on 21 October the grid-pipeline note records zero grid jobs run, gate words under review in PR #54 and one press by the owner outstanding, with a schedule of first shards 23 Oct, version 1 trained 28 Oct, latency 29 Oct, provisional filed 30 Oct and the CNS mini-oral 2 Nov, and the RSNA RATIC link expiring 2026-10-28. The seed grant (aidas-seed-grant-proposal) was due October 16, 2026, now past, with the submission address, PI, case count and the $24/h rate still '[to confirm]', biosketches undrafted, refiner results 'pending' that the proposal already tabled, and a manuscript 'in preparation' that the 8 October handoff says is held pending the technology-transfer office, with the disclosure filed 2026-09-25 and no provisional recorded. The retrospective protocol is 'Date Submitted: Draft', expects AIDaS notification December 16, 2026 and a January 2027 start, and leaves frames per case and the verification fraction to a 20-case pilot; the older eProtocol draft of 15 September 2026 carries '40,000 studies — unconfirmed', '7 years — confirm', citations to insert and a pending trauma co-investigator. Neither protocol nor the grant mentions the HPR 2026-330 supplement of 29 September that the atlas records, and the atlas (17 October) still asks whether DUA data needs its own determination. The atlas lists eleven unsent Outlook drafts and an unconfirmed USD 250 Radiopaedia fee; the grid note says the Radiopaedia licence waits on countersignature and JHU had not replied on 21 October; the handoff of 8 October had the cine-source letters 'drafted; none sent'. The research-directions note (8 October) counts zero verified transitional real-frame test persons against 35 needed, while vertebral-levels-without-ct (18 September) had a 376-patient transitional cross-validation 'running now'; counting-from-the-sacrum and what-is-left-after-physics (22 September) describe training and measurements in progress whose results no cluster artifact reports. The lab recipe notes the public mirror still at v10 on 2026-09-27 and weights shipped on the website until 2026-09-14. The outreach note read funder pages in September 2026 and expects RSNA cycles to open in October. The lift-before-label note's verification pass never ran and it still expects registered frames from the older Protocol 1 design; the fluorocap note has the PACS capture object type undetermined and FluoroCap QC pending on all 21,603 rows.
result.notes: All nineteen records were read in full except SchwingNet__fluorocap-reality-check-czudvb.json, read to line 1053 of 1290 (the unread tail is the end of external_sources and the trailing metadata). Quotes are taken from the records' quote fields; the artifacts' plain text under scratchpad/text/SchwingNet/ was not consulted. Two quotes are paraphrases of record decision fields rather than page text: the grant's 'not eligible to serve as PI' and the older draft's 'a first-year surgery resident at DMC'. Items noted but not listed as candidates: the atlas's own open question of 13 versus 6 Balgrist specimens (letter versus paper) sits inside one artifact; the CNS dates '2 Nov, mini-oral 66629' and '31 Oct to 4 Nov 2026' are a day and a meeting range, not a conflict; Manbachi 2018 is quoted as 30.4%/2.4% error in two notes and 69.6%/97.6% correct in another, which agree; LSTV prevalence appears as 15.3% (83 studies), 12.9% of lumbar surgical patients, 15-25%, and 9-11% count-changing types II-IV, which are different quantities but will confuse a stratum definition; the registration-free feasibility note (15 September) says no surviving claim gives wrong-level incidence, which the later documents take from Furuya 2026 rather than from that verified set. The detector field report says none of its tests are cross-site and recall is not reported globally by design, while the proposal, grant and protocol quote 99.14% per-body recall; whether that is the same detector is not established by the records. People are named by role throughout; no contact details appear in the records' quotes used here.

result.cluster: FluoroCap: the corpus, its pipeline and its audits

verdicts.topic: Figure-mate region agreement with constraint decoding versus the level model alone (same corpus, same date, 2026-09-14)
verdicts.quote_a: "figure mates agreeing on region (decoder)", "88%", "panels of the same figure with the same caption levels; 52% for the model alone (partly induced by the shared caption)"
verdicts.quote_b: Constraint decoding lifts caption-free region agreement from 52.1% to 91.5% and the rate of substantially overlapping level sets from 30.8% to 68.2%.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 14 Sep. The card's 88% is a string typed into its script, not computed from its data, and it gives no pair count. The card's own data does hold the model-alone figure (468 pairs, 52.1%, recurrent_pred), which matches the audit. Only the decoder figure differs: 88% on the card against 91.5% on 519 pairs in the audit. The card also says the model-alone figure is 'partly induced by the shared caption', but the audit says no caption enters the check. The reality check (15 Sep) repeats 91.5% and 52.1% on 519 and 468 pairs, and labels them model-versus-model agreement.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 91.5% (519 pairs) for the decoder and 52.1% (468 pairs) for the model alone, as agreement between automatic sources rather than accuracy. Mark the card's 88% as a typed number with no source. Regenerating the card from the decode's consistency file would settle the figure.

verdicts.topic: What the panels without a vertebra box are: detector misses or non-radiographs
verdicts.quote_a: The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
verdicts.quote_b: The modality classifier scored 18,119 unique panels: 5,665 (31%) more likely a spine radiograph than not, 2,991 (17%) at p ≥ 0.7, 895 (5%) at p ≥ 0.9; 8,843 (49%) score as not an x-ray at all.
verdicts.explanation: The audit (14 Sep) infers that most of the missing panels are detector misses, without scoring them. The reality check (15 Sep) scored 18,119 panels with the classifier (panel_preds.jsonl, read at 07:30): 49% score as not an x-ray, and 35% of the level-labelled decoded panels are not spine radiographs. It also says the 93% was not measured on FluoroCap panels. The corpus grew with the refetch re-split between the two pages, but the later page measured what the earlier one only inferred. Both readings rest on one classifier that was never tested on mined figures.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the reality check's measured purity, with its file and time, and drop the audit's inference. How much of the no-box set is detector miss stays unmeasured until a human reads a stratified sample of those panels.

verdicts.topic: The 2,143-panel held-out set behind the 93% modality score: FluoroCap panels or film-manifest classes
verdicts.quote_a: The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
verdicts.quote_b: | 93.1% modality head / 99.5% view head | | 2,143 / 800 held-out | | film-manifest classes | | not FluoroCap panels; modality is "unknown" for 7,642 of 17,486 manifest rows |
verdicts.explanation: The later page names the test set behind the 93% as film-manifest classes and says outright that it is not FluoroCap panels. The audit called the same items 'panels' and applied the score to FluoroCap. The card's own data (14 Sep) gives a third version of the modality head: 94.0% on 2,843 held out, with class counts 23,571 / 395 / 4,469. Neither page has a score on mined figures.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry: 93.1% on 2,143 held-out film-manifest items, not FluoroCap panels. The classifier is unvalidated on the corpus until a labelled FluoroCap sample is scored, and the book should name which classifier version each number belongs to.

verdicts.topic: Caption-held-out accuracy of the level model alone, and containment of its level set
verdicts.quote_a: The level model alone is right 38.3% of the time on panels where the caption was held back.
verdicts.quote_b: | 57.1% containment, Jaccard 0.341 | | 380 "caption-free" panels | | caption-derived | | not a random hold-out: hard_caption is False exactly when the caption's levels did not fit any contiguous window over the detected boxes |
verdicts.explanation: The audit gives 38.3% (n = 175 in its script data) and 56.8% containment (n = 389, Jaccard 0.34). The next day's reality check gives 37.9% on 169 and 57.1% on 380 (Jaccard 0.341). The caption-constrained count also moves, from 1,678 to 1,615. The later page re-read the decode and adds that the caption-free subset is chosen by caption-detector misfit, so it is not a random hold-out and its labels are captions.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the reality check's numbers together with its caveat, and present neither pair as an accuracy. The random draw on the level verification bench, once it has been read, gives the first accuracy estimate.

verdicts.topic: Where every panel comes from: open-licence published figures only, or also surgical video frames
verdicts.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
verdicts.quote_b: The corpus is eleven thousand panel images mined from the literature and from surgical video.
verdicts.explanation: The card describes manifest v0.2: 10,281 rows, dataset_version 0.2, with no YouTube route in its data. Its section 11 says video-frame panels belong to version 0.3, which is still in progress. The audit counts every panel image on disk (11,349, including 479 video frames), not the card's release. Read in context, the card does not say video frames do not exist. Its provenance sentence does fail for other reasons, though: its own manifest lists 42 Reddit rows and 246 panels with an unknown licence (see the next candidate).
verdicts.resolution_hint: Limit the card's provenance sentence to the v0.2 manifest of figure panels. State separately that the corpus on disk also holds YouTube frames that are not openly licensed (479 on 14 Sep, 1,096 plus 366 on 15 Sep, 2,535 on 16 Sep).

verdicts.topic: Provenance of the corpus versus the closed-journal refetch and the Instagram harvest
verdicts.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
verdicts.quote_b: The refetch touches only the closed-journal figures that already carry a matched caption (about 600), one request every three seconds per host, capped per day, never full text or PDFs in bulk.
verdicts.explanation: The access setup (14 Sep, afternoon) says closed-journal figures are already in the corpus. It plans to refetch them through the institutional route, and to harvest Instagram under a dedicated account even though Meta's terms forbid automated collection. The overnight report confirms the proxy session served 653 figures and the Instagram route ran. The card's own data also contradicts its blanket open-licence sentence: its routes include reddit (42) and openalex_pdf (41), Dataset A has 246 'unknown' licences, and 166 panels are in tier E. 'Institutional image' in the card means patient images from an institution, not library access, so the conflict is about the open-licence claim and whether the panels can be redistributed.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Withdraw the card's open-licence sentence. Carry the later records: the licence is 'the publishers' (figures)' (registry) and 'figure reuse only, never redistributed' (atlas), and the corpus holds closed-journal copies fetched through the WSU proxy plus Instagram and Reddit images.

verdicts.topic: Rule for sources whose terms forbid automated collection
verdicts.quote_a: Meta's terms prohibit automated collection. Accounts used for it get action-blocked, then disabled. Use a dedicated account, not the one attached to your name or practice.
verdicts.quote_b: never scored; private tracker screening only, never training or a slide; the YouTube copies are unpermitted until a request is answered
verdicts.explanation: The access setup (14 Sep) plans scripted Instagram collection while knowing the terms forbid it. The registry (20 Oct) takes the opposite line. It treats the YouTube copies as unpermitted until the uploader answers, and it records Radiopaedia as 'no scraping' because of its licence terms. The Honest 99 report also left Radiopaedia and Eurorad unscraped because of their AI-training signals. These are two practices for one situation, and the later one is stricter. The registry quotes come from the page source, because the plain-text export cuts off the record array.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the later rule: no scripted collection where a platform's terms forbid it, and copies already taken are held for private screening only until permission arrives. This matches the project decision that Radiopaedia is never fetched by script. Record a status for the 1,633 Instagram images, which no page gives one.

verdicts.topic: Releasing FluoroCap (Dataset A and B licence tiers) versus the private-forever rule
verdicts.quote_a: Two releases from one manifest: Dataset A (all open-access licence tiers, research use) and Dataset B (CC BY, CC0 and public-domain panels only).
verdicts.quote_b: Level-identification code, FluoroCap, model weights, spinesurg-ct-nnunet, XRSpinoPelvic1K. Never in a public repository, never on the website.
verdicts.explanation: The card (14 Sep) is written as a release card, with redistribution fields, licence tiers, a commercial-training flag and example sections. The lab recipe (27 Sep) lists FluoroCap as private forever, and the handoff's rule 8 says the same. The card never says 'public' in so many words. The atlas (17 Oct) shows the frozen v0.1 A and B exist as internal versions that are 'never redistributed'. So the A/B split survives internally, and the public-release reading is overruled.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the private-forever rule. Describe Datasets A and B as internal frozen versions. Any public release would need a new decision from the owner.

verdicts.topic: Whether FluoroCap may train the level model
verdicts.quote_a: That is the correct signal that constraint decoding is doing real work — and it is also the reason this corpus must not be used to retrain the level model without re-weighting, because the model would be learning largely from its own errors.
verdicts.quote_b: Tier 4, the mined figures and video: an external test set only, after a two-reader read of a stratified sample, and a source for the modality and hardware heads; never for the level head.
verdicts.explanation: The audit allows retraining if the data are re-weighted. A day later the reality check lists 'Training or fine-tuning any level head on caption-derived labels' under what to stop. The handoff (8 Oct) and the registry (20 Oct) record directive D1: FluoroCap is out of training. The audit's own section 5 already says re-weighting cannot help classes that have no examples.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry directive D1: FluoroCap may be a test set at most and is never training data. Add the handoff's finding that the old C-ArmLSpine fold banks still held FluoroCap crops.

verdicts.topic: FluoroCap crops still in the C-ArmLSpine fold banks despite the directive
verdicts.quote_a: The C-ArmLSpine fold models behind the fine-tuned naming numbers still train on 2,632 VinDr crops and 2,100 FluoroCap crops per fold bank, plus both NHANES copies, because the v9-initialised fold models reuse fold banks built from allspine\_v7.
verdicts.quote_b: out of training by directive D1; a test set at most; still inside the old fold banks
verdicts.explanation: Read whole in the page source (the plain-text export cuts off the record array), the registry's FluoroCap status ends 'still inside the old fold banks'. That is exactly what the handoff found. The candidate quoted only the first half. The two pages agree that D1 is the rule and that the old fold banks still break it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both: D1 is the rule, and the fine-tuned C-ArmLSpine numbers come from fold banks that still hold FluoroCap and VinDr. Clean fold models exist (the Figure 5b name_fill cells, per the handoff), and retraining the fold models on clean banks closes the gap.

verdicts.topic: The 99% selective-accuracy claim and its held-out status
verdicts.quote_a: It is measured on held-out renders, which is stated wherever it appears, and the real-film version needs the calibration set described in section 4.
verdicts.quote_b: The consequences: allspine v2, v6 and v7, anchor\_drr and vindrps are leaked families, and every number from them is record only, including the 99.02 % shortcut-free film number and the 99 % selective-accuracy claim.
verdicts.explanation: The handoff (8 Oct) records the NHANES double entry found on 2026-09-22 and rules the allspine_v2 family leaked. It names the 99% selective-accuracy claim as record only, and its catalog part C says the number comes from the leaked allspine_v2 bank. That plainly revises the Honest 99 report's 'held-out' wording of 16 Sep.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the 99% as record only, because it comes from a leaked bank. Any selective-accuracy claim must be rerun on the G3 person-disjoint split and pass through the evaluation gate before it is quoted.

verdicts.topic: How many panels were decoded and labelled before 2026-09-16 (the baseline the Honest 99 report compares against)
verdicts.quote_a: 20,700 panels decoded and 11,377 carrying a level, against 5,789 and 4,614 yesterday morning.
verdicts.quote_b: Three thousand of them carry machine-assigned vertebra labels.
verdicts.explanation: The audit (14 Sep) and the reality check (15 Sep, 06:55 to 07:35) both read the 14 Sep decode. It ran 3,294 panels, about 3,000 of them unique and labelled, and the reality check counts 2,071 decoded panels with level labels. The overnight report shows a preview decode (tag v3pre) starting at 08:14 on 15 Sep with the v2 model. The Honest 99 baseline of 5,789 and 4,614 'yesterday morning' may be that decode, which no page reports. The texts neither confirm nor contradict the baseline.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Find the decode file behind 5,789 and 4,614 (probably the v3pre decode_v2 output of 15 Sep) and name it. Until then, cite each decoded count with its decode tag and time.

verdicts.topic: Whether any real panel carries an L6 or T13 label
verdicts.quote_b: | L6 | | 0 panels labelled; 0 real-film crops | | 802 crops from at most 90 distinct cases (56 VerSe + 34 CTSP); 13 in val |
verdicts.explanation: The 15 Sep zero was read from a decode whose decoder could not output L6 or T13; the overnight report says that column read 0.0% 'by construction'. That morning the decoder was changed to try a column with a T13 or an L6 inserted, against a prior penalty. The Honest 99 table counts machine labels from the 16 Sep decode of 20,700 panels. Neither page reports a human-read L6 or T13, and the handoff (8 Oct) still counts 0 verified real-frame transitional test persons. Nothing explains the 145 'caption-named' L6 panels, given that the reality check found only 22 plus 20 transitional-caption figures, mostly from animals.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the 16 Sep counts as decoder placements that no human has checked, and state that no real panel carries a human-verified L6 or T13. Reading the 338 L6 and 254 T13 panels, or the transitional bench, would settle whether any real positive exists.

verdicts.topic: Real L6 cases available for a transitional test
verdicts.quote_a: yes, lumbar, projected from the CBCT (two labellers agreeing on 814 of 910 bodies); 3 real L6 cases
verdicts.quote_b: 0 verified real-frame transitional test persons against 35 needed
verdicts.explanation: The registry (page source) records three L6 cases in C-ArmLSpine, with labels projected from the CBCT. The handoff counts verified, error-free transitional test persons for its power argument. Both can hold if the three are unverified, or if they sit in the encoder's training lineage: the handoff says 92 of 97 transitional validation and test persons do. Neither page says which applies.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Check the registry record's sources (DATA.md and DATASET_USAGE.md 2.1) and the handoff's RESULTS_CATALOG part A, to see whether the three C-ArmLSpine L6 cases are verified and held out. Until then, write '3 L6 cases, unverified, not counted as test persons'.

verdicts.topic: Images on disk after the refetch (figure panels, video, video-medium)
verdicts.quote_a: Images on disk went from 11,349 to 19,048: 17,755 figure panels (10,870 before the 1,167 round-one figures were re-split), 927 video panels and 366 medium-confidence video panels.
verdicts.quote_b: | Panel images on disk | | 19,581 (18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium) | | find on ~/FluoroCap; morning report's 19,048 superseded |
verdicts.explanation: The reality check counted the files with find at about 07:00 on 15 Sep and states that the morning report's 19,048 is superseded. The overnight report's 08:30 update left its 02:21 count unchanged.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 19,581 (18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium) as of 15 Sep at about 07:00, with how it was counted. Later counts (Honest 99, atlas) supersede it in turn.

verdicts.topic: Corpus size over time: 11,349 to 19,581 to 20,700 decoded to 29,500 panels
verdicts.quote_a: 19,581 (18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium)
verdicts.quote_b: 29,500 panels (png); manifest 21,603 rows keyed by about 1,197-1,953 source documents (no patient key); frozen v0.1 A 2,531 / B 991 panels; YouTube 298,075 frames; 316 GB tree
verdicts.explanation: These are successive snapshots of a corpus that kept growing, not a conflict. The Honest 99 report has 20,700 decoded panels on 16 Sep. The atlas (as of 17 Oct; quote from the page source, because the text export cuts off its data) gives 29,500 panels and 21,603 manifest rows, and the registry (20 Oct) repeats 29,500.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the atlas and registry counts as current, and date every earlier count. Name the command behind 29,500 (presumably a find on the grid tree), which neither page states.

verdicts.topic: Closed-journal refetch: figures replaced and pixel gain
verdicts.quote_a: 1,489 of 2,901 figures replaced with the publisher's larger copy, median 6.3× the pixels; round two still running
verdicts.quote_b: | Publisher-original refetch | | 1,558 of 2,901 figures replaced (53.7%); pixel-area gain p50 6.26× (≈ 2.5× linear); new short side p50 1,254 vs old 474; 1,343 misses led by DOI prefixes 10.4103 (158), 10.1097 (123), 10.1186 (81); 931 "no candidate served" | | ~/FluoroCap_wsl/refetch_hires.jsonl, round two still running; morning report's 1,489 superseded |
verdicts.explanation: The reality check explicitly replaces 1,489 with 1,558, read from refetch_hires.jsonl. The Honest 99 report (16 Sep) then says 'Round two replaced 2,059 figures with publisher originals at a median of 6.25 times the pixels.' All three are counts of a job that was still running.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 2,059 (16 Sep) as the latest count, noting that no page marks it final, and cite refetch_hires.jsonl. Treat 1,489 and 1,558 as intermediate.

verdicts.topic: Video panels in the corpus
verdicts.quote_a: Images on disk went from 11,349 to 19,048: 17,755 figure panels (10,870 before the 1,167 round-one figures were re-split), 927 video panels and 366 medium-confidence video panels.
verdicts.quote_b: 19,581 (18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium)
verdicts.explanation: The reality check's count was taken later that morning and explicitly supersedes the overnight report's total. The Honest 99 report then counts 2,535 video frames by route on 16 Sep.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 1,096 video and 366 video-medium for the morning of 15 Sep, and 2,535 video frames for 16 Sep, each with its date.

verdicts.topic: Manifest rows and dataset version
verdicts.quote_a: "manifest_rows": 10281, "manifest_version": "1.1", "dataset_version": "0.2"
verdicts.quote_b: In the released manifest of 17,486 rows, 9,036 sit below the 0.3 floor, 4,218 pass the default inclusion rules, and human_qc_status reads pending on every row.
verdicts.explanation: The card was generated at 09:43 on 2026-09-14 from a manifest of 10,281 rows. The reality check (15 Sep) reads a manifest of 17,486 rows, made after the refetch re-split, and the atlas (17 Oct) reads 21,603 rows. These are successive manifests, and the card is a snapshot.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Quote the card's counts only with its generation time. Carry 21,603 rows (17 Oct) as current, and regenerate the card from the current manifest if it is to be cited.

verdicts.topic: Which manifest version the pipeline produces on 2026-09-14
verdicts.quote_a: refresh orchestrator\nwindow search → panels → scoring → manifest v0.3
verdicts.quote_b: Version 0.3 is in progress: video-frame panels with spoken-level cues, archive scans, technique guides and teaching-case sites; they enter the manifest with the same fields and tiers.
verdicts.explanation: The map is a design diagram of what the refresh orchestrator will write. The card says v0.3 is in progress. Nothing on the map claims that v0.3 had already been produced, so the two agree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Cite the map for the pipeline's target (v0.3) and the card for the version actually produced on 14 Sep (dataset_version 0.2, manifest 1.1).

verdicts.topic: State of the all-spine v2 model on 2026-09-15
verdicts.quote_a: | All-spine v2 on renders or transitional strata | | absent | | — | | weights destroyed by the chain's link step; retrain 40285209 pending at read time |
verdicts.quote_b: Its diagnostic now excludes renders of training cases (a filter added this morning): over 800 held-out renders it scores 64.2% , with 4,505 training renders skipped.
verdicts.explanation: The reality check's snapshot (06:55 to 07:35) predates the overnight report's 08:13 update. By then the resubmitted v2 retrain had registered as allspine_v2_r1 and scored 64.2% on 800 held-out renders. The reality check itself lists 'Whether the v2 retrain landed' as an open question. The handoff later rules allspine v2 a leaked family, so every number from it, this one included, is record only.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry: v2 retrained and registered at 08:13 on 15 Sep (allspine_v2_r1), 64.2% on 800 renders with training cases excluded. Mark it record only, following the handoff's leak ruling on allspine v2.

verdicts.topic: Design of the reference standard: two blind readers with adjudication, or one reader
verdicts.quote_a: The protocol specifies two readers blind to each other and to the proposal, adjudication of disagreements by a third, and locking of the dataset, the model and the analysis plan before any performance claim.
verdicts.quote_b: This panel has no caption naming a level. Your read is the only ground truth it will ever have.
verdicts.explanation: The bench stores one read per panel, keyed only by image id, in a shared store (db.doc("reads/"+it.image_id).set(rec)), and loads everyone's reads when it opens. A second reader would therefore see and overwrite the first: the tool can keep neither two blind reads nor a third reader's adjudication. The card's protocol is not what the built tool runs.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Describe the built bench as single-read. Before inter-reader agreement can be reported, reads must be keyed by reader and a separate adjudication pass added.

verdicts.topic: How many panels must be read to turn agreement into accuracy
verdicts.quote_a: Read 400 panels. Nothing else converts an agreement number into an accuracy number.
verdicts.quote_b: The QC's own arithmetic says 545 reads for ±3% around 85%; bounding 99% within ±0.5% takes about 1,500 verified images per stratum you report on (Wilson), and the primary strata are at least four (lumbosacral normal, lumbosacral LSTV, thoracolumbar, hardware).
verdicts.explanation: Both pages agree that 196 reads give ±5% and 545 give ±3%. The audit picked 400 as its action. A day later the reality check sets a two-reader read of the 545-panel set for weeks 1 and 2. Its 1,500 per stratum is a separate target: bounding a 99% claim, which in its design is measured on real Tier 0 frames. The later page raises the FluoroCap read from 400 to 545.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 545 two-reader, adjudicated FluoroCap reads (±3% around 85%) as the read target, and 1,500 verified vertebrae per primary stratum for any 99% claim. Note that the benches built hold 120 and 179 panels.

verdicts.topic: Jecklin 2024 real-image recovery number
verdicts.quote_a: The registered pairs are worth more as labelled fine-tuning data than as anything else: a DRR-only model that collapsed on real frames recovered to F1 0.84 against a 0.86 DRR ceiling with 3,317 registered real crops, and paired pix2pix translation on the same pairs gave the identical 0.84 (Jecklin 2024); where paired and unpaired translation were compared head to head the paired route bought at most one point (86.8% vs 85.8% registration success).
verdicts.quote_b: Outside the project, no paper tests a DRR-trained vertebra-level classifier on real fluoroscopy; the nearest discrete-label precedents lose 26-28 points (Pelphix) and 9 points (SyntheX's lesion task, which is segmentation accuracy, not classification: SyntheX has no classification task), and Jecklin 2024 needed 3,317 pose-paired real frames from 10 cadavers to lift lumbar reconstruction from a surface score of 0.08 back to 0.63-0.73, still below its 0.79 DRR ceiling, with no intermediate sizes tested.
verdicts.explanation: The pages quote two metrics: F1 0.84 against a 0.86 ceiling, and a surface score going from 0.08 to 0.63-0.73 against a 0.79 ceiling. Both may appear in the paper; Lift itself also quotes a surface score ('one case 8% against 76% on its DRR twin'). The texts do not settle whether these measure one quantity. Lift's verification pass never ran, while the reality check's literature claims went through a refutation pass.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Read Jecklin 2024's results table. Until then, prefer the reality check's verified surface-score figures, and name the metric beside each number.

verdicts.topic: Literature results on synthetic-to-real transfer (DeepDRR 78.2 to 24.7 mm, SyntheX 5.95 vs 6.46 mm)
verdicts.quote_a: (1) Physics in the renderer: naive DRRs to DeepDRR took landmark error on real cadaver films from 78.2 to 24.7 mm ( Unberath 2019 ); strong domain randomisation on 10,000 DRRs from 20 CTs beat training on the 366 real frames (5.95 vs 6.46 mm) and CycleGAN or ADDA added nothing on top (SyntheX).
verdicts.quote_b: Physics matters more than volume at the start: the same landmark network went from 78.2 mm to 24.7 mm mean error on 78 real cadaver X-rays when naive DRRs were replaced by DeepDRRs, most of the gain arriving before scatter was added ("Enabling machine learning in X-ray-based procedures via realistic simulation of image formation", pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov ).
verdicts.explanation: The 78.2 to 24.7 mm result matches on both pages. The SyntheX 5.95 against 6.46 mm also appears on both, but the reality check's verified text corrects Lift's reading of it. It says the scaled set is reported as both 10,000 and 18,000 images, and that 'scale rather than the strong-randomisation list is what carried the win'. So the shared block agrees on the numbers but not on what SyntheX shows.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the reality check's verified wording for SyntheX: scale, 10,000 or 18,000 images, and a scaling curve that is not monotone. Correct Lift's unverified attribution of the win to strong randomisation.
