verdicts.topic: Number of lumbar-rib cases in CTSpinoPelvic1K (802 records)
verdicts.quote_a: The model never memorises sixteen lumbar-rib examples in order to recognise one.
verdicts.quote_b: The 13 cases carrying a rib on a lumbar body cluster at four, as they must.
verdicts.explanation: Both statements are in their texts and give different counts for the same class in the same 802-record corpus: sixteen on the design page (which says its counts are from 'the released labels', release unnamed), 13 on the border page (v5_final, after a rib renumbering that gave lumbar ribs their own class). The border page also says 'the only reader disagreement of the fourteen' about its lumbar-rib set, so it carries 13 and 14 itself. Neither page says which label release or which rule its count comes from. Both pages are undated.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry one count of lumbar-rib cases from the current label release (v11 per the 2026-10-08 pages), with the rule stated (rib articulating with a lumbar body, by case). A recount on v11 settles it; until then the book should give 13 (v5, renumbered) and 16 (release unnamed) side by side with their sources.

verdicts.topic: Number of lumbar ribs in CTSpinoPelvic1K: strict-incidence count versus ribs-on-a-lumbar-vertebra count versus short-rib count
verdicts.quote_a: Proximity is not articulation: a 12th rib head at the T12/L1 junction is within 10 mm of both, and that marked L1 rib‑bearing in 61 cases where the strict incidence QC found only 14 lumbar ribs in the entire cohort.
verdicts.quote_b: ribs at or under 50 mm: 152 twelfth against 10 lumbar
verdicts.explanation: The figures count different things. The research-directions page's 10 is lumbar ribs at or under 50 mm (a length-filtered subset), and its CT-8 '30 read positives' is the n of a study first calibrated on VerSe masks, not a CTSpinoPelvic1K count. Inside the audit, 14 'lumbar ribs' (set against 61 cases) and the incidence table's 21 then 25 ribs 'on a lumbar vertebra' may be cases versus ribs, which the page does not say. Nothing in the texts settles whether any two of these are the same quantity.
verdicts.resolution_hint: A single table on the current release giving lumbar-rib cases and lumbar ribs (left and right), with the length-filtered and read subsets as named rows, would settle it. Until then the book should label each figure with its unit and rule rather than treat them as rival counts.

verdicts.topic: Lumbar-rib count in the project's own CTs as tabled for training
verdicts.quote_a: | lumbar rib | | 16 | | — | | — | | 16 | | single source, and it disagrees with its own review sheet |
verdicts.quote_b: The 13 cases carrying a rib on a lumbar body cluster at four, as they must.
verdicts.explanation: The overnight page (2026-09-16) tables 16 lumbar-rib cases in the project's CTs and itself says the source disagrees with its review sheet. The undated border page gives 13 cases with a rib on a lumbar body after its renumbering. Its row 'Lumbar ribs still mislabelled "rib 12" | 14 | 1' counts mislabelled ribs, not the total. The two counts disagree and neither reconciles them.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Recount lumbar-rib cases on the release the training actually uses (v11), and give the review sheet's count beside it. The book should not carry 16 as a training denominator without the overnight page's own warning attached.

verdicts.topic: Co-occurrence of thoracolumbar and lumbosacral variants within CTSpinoPelvic1K (the both-cell and its odds ratio)
verdicts.quote_a: Cases with a thoracolumbar variant carry a lumbosacral variant 44 times, where independence predicts 9. Of 796 cases with complete measurements: 667 typical at both ends, 60 thoracolumbar only, 25 lumbosacral only, 44 both.
verdicts.quote_b: CTSpinoPelvic1K 4.00 [1.00, 16.03] on a both-cell of two.
verdicts.explanation: Same cohort, same question, and the both-cell is 44 (OR 19.6) on the border page against 2 (OR 4.00) on the naming page (2026-09-17). The naming page says its flags were read from label voxels (T13, lumbar rib, or rib-bearing count not 12 where the field reached rib 12) and that the abdominopelvic scans cannot see the upper ribs. The border page's text never says how it defines a thoracolumbar variant. Its figure caption lists a rib 12/11 length-ratio panel, so a segmentation-derived rib measure is the likely basis, but the text does not settle that.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The book should carry the naming page's label-voxel figure with its definition, and present the border page's 19.6 only with its definition stated and its own caveat ('an association in segmentation-derived measures'). Running both flag definitions on the same v11 labels and tabling the 2x2 for each would settle it.

verdicts.topic: Strength of thoracolumbar-lumbosacral co-occurrence used as the programme's number
verdicts.quote_a: This is the “one population, not two” claim, made countable.
verdicts.quote_b: On the 280 subjects with both ends graded: OR 3.61, exact 95% CI [2.08, 6.27]; with morphology-only flags 3.2 [1.8, 5.8]; on the 115 with both junctions in the field 2.1 [0.9, 5.0].
verdicts.explanation: The border page headlines OR 19.6 as 'strongly'. The naming page's hypothesis table calls co-occurrence 'supported, smaller than first tabulated'. It gives 3.61 on VerSe and 4.00 on CTSpinoPelvic1K, notes that its all-rows 4.30 was inflated by count-coupling, and puts published series at 1.9-13.7. The research-directions page uses 'the VerSe odds ratio 3.61' as its outside check. The 19.6 is above every figure in the naming page's range.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the naming page's graded estimates (3.61 VerSe, 2.1 with both junctions in field, 4.00 CTSpinoPelvic1K) as the programme's number. Report 19.6 only as a segmentation-derived association under its own definition. CT-3's whole-cohort read is the planned test that settles it on CTSpinoPelvic1K.

verdicts.topic: Count of thoracolumbar-variant spines in CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_a: Of 796 cases with complete measurements: 667 typical at both ends, 60 thoracolumbar only, 25 lumbosacral only, 44 both.
verdicts.quote_b: Using the CT flag table, spines were classed as ordinary (902), lumbosacral-only (98), thoracolumbar-only (47), or both (66)—the both-cell was two when the labels came from one cohort of 802 abdominopelvic scans that cannot see the upper ribs.
verdicts.explanation: The border page finds 104 thoracolumbar-variant spines (60 + 44) in 796 CTSpinoPelvic1K cases. The naming page finds 113 (47 + 66) across 1,113 spines that include those 802 plus 311 VerSe, and only 2 'both' in CTSpinoPelvic1K. So the border page's 60 thoracolumbar-only cases outnumber the naming page's 47 in all sources. The two pages must define a thoracolumbar variant differently, and neither text puts the definitions side by side.
verdicts.resolution_hint: State one definition of a thoracolumbar variant (label-voxel T13, lumbar rib or rib count, as on the naming page, or a rib-12 length threshold) and recount CTSpinoPelvic1K under it. The book should not merge the two counts.

verdicts.topic: Distribution of the non-rib-bearing vertebra count (cases at four) in CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_b: The cohort piles at five ( 734 cases). Labelled LSTV cases sit at four ( 35 ) and six ( 26 ) instead — sacralization pulling one way, lumbarization the other.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages work on v5 and agree on 734 at five and 26 at six, but the four-cell is 26 in the audit and 35 on the border page. Read as cell totals, 35 conflicts with the audit's 26. Read literally as LSTV-labelled cases, 35 + 26 = 61 exceeds the border page's own 33 non-normal labels. The border page's renumbering ('finished alongside this') might have moved cases into the four-cell, but neither text says so. The research-directions CT-7 cells (26 transitional at counts 4 and 6, 757 normal at 4 and 5, 7 transitional at 5, 9 normal at 6) use yet another partition.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Recompute the count histogram on the current release with the audit's nearest-vertebra rib-bearing rule, crossed with the LSTV label. Carry the audit's caveat that the distribution largely reflects the label convention.

verdicts.topic: Whether the non-rib-bearing vertebra count carries the lumbosacral phenotype
verdicts.quote_a: The 93.3 / 3.3 / 3.3 distribution above should not be quoted as a phenotype prevalence.
verdicts.quote_b: | n_non_rib_bearing | | 0.8 | | The classic count, earning its reputation |
verdicts.explanation: The measured facts do not clash: the audit scores the count against a radiologist's own count (2 of 22 agree), and the border page scores it against the LSTV label (d 0.8). The readings do clash. The audit says the count 'recovers the labelling convention, not the patient', while the border page says it is 'earning its reputation'. Since the count is derived from labels that encode LSTV (the border page's has_l6_label scores d 4.7), the d of 0.8 may be the circularity the audit describes. Neither page addresses the other.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the audit's verdict and its radiologist comparison. Present the border page's d 0.8 only as separation of a label from a measure derived from the same labels. Rescoring the count against the readers' Lumbosac.csv column on the current release would settle whether the verdict still stands.

verdicts.topic: Whether ribs inform the lumbosacral junction
verdicts.quote_a: But this dataset’s transitional cases live at the lumbosacral junction, and ribs say nothing there.
verdicts.quote_b: Ranked by standardised difference against the LSTV label, rib12_len_left_mm clears d = 0.5 — a measurement taken at the other end of the spine from the thing being labelled.
verdicts.explanation: In context, the audit's sentence is about rib-bearing grouping as a counting anchor: ribs cannot locate the lumbosacral boundary. The border page reports a modest statistical association (d 0.55) between rib-12 length and the LSTV label, which it attributes to co-occurrence. An association does not locate the junction, so the two claims can both hold. The prose 'clears d = 0.5' and the table's 0.55 are consistent.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The book can carry both, each with its scope: ribs do not anchor the lumbosacral count, and rib-12 length is weakly associated with the LSTV label through co-occurrence. Drop the unqualified 'ribs say nothing there'.

verdicts.topic: Whether the CTSpinoPelvic1K label volume ever carries a sixth lumbar vertebra
verdicts.quote_a: The count is derived from labelled vertebrae, and the label volume assigns L1–L5 plus a sacrum regardless of the true anatomy.
verdicts.quote_b: | has_l6_label | | 4.7 | | A sixth lumbar label is nearly definitional |
verdicts.explanation: The border page, on the same v5_final data, uses an L6-label indicator as a measure. The state-of-the-literature page (2026-10-08) counts 18 L6 by release label, and the research-directions page lists Dataset813 with 18 L6. The audit's own v5 histogram puts 26 cases at six non-rib-bearing vertebrae, which a label volume stopping at L5 could not produce. Read literally, the audit's sentence is contradicted, including by its own table. It may mean that most transitional cases are labelled L1-L5, but it does not say so.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Correct the audit's sentence to say that most, not all, transitional cases are labelled L1-L5 plus sacrum, and carry the L6 label count (18 by release label on v11) beside it.

verdicts.topic: Why sacral foramina fail as an anchor on CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_a: The measurement is dominated by field of view — many sacra are truncated inferiorly in an abdominal CT.
verdicts.quote_b: The detector does not deliver it. On one symmetric sacrum it returned 3 left and 7 right.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages rule the foramina anchor out. One names inferior truncation of the field as the main cause and the other names detector defects (closing canals, invented ones). Neither page denies the other's cause, so the two explanations are complementary, not contradictory.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both causes together. Whether a better detector would rescue the anchor is open, and would be settled by running a revised detector on the subset whose sacrum is wholly inside the field.

verdicts.topic: Four pairs of sacral foramina is normal and five means the sacrum absorbed a lumbar segment
verdicts.quote_a: Sacral foramina are the textbook sacrum-intrinsic anchor — four pairs is normal, five means it absorbed a lumbar segment — and would be an ideal anchor C, needing no reference to the ilium.
verdicts.quote_b: Intended as the measure that settles sacralization without trusting any vertebra label — four pairs normal, five means the sacrum absorbed L5.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages state the rule with no citation, and both then find the corpus mode at three (the design page's normal-labelled distribution; the border page sets its reference box 'to the cohort mode rather than a textbook 4').
verdicts.resolution_hint: Cite an anatomy reference for the four-pair rule before the book states it. Report the corpus mode of three as an effect of truncation and the detector, not as anatomy.

verdicts.topic: The ilium's auricular surface and the sacroiliac articulation are unchanged by lumbosacral fusion and can anchor sacralisation
verdicts.quote_a: The auricular surface belongs to the ilium and is not relinquished when a lumbar segment fuses above it.
verdicts.quote_b: One scalar per case: tight in normal anatomy, shifted by about a segment in transitional.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages treat the sacroiliac articulation as a label-independent anchor and state the premise with no source. The audit also asserts 'Castellvi II–IV by definition' for ilium contact without a citation. Neither page measures the premise. The nearest measurement in the cluster, the border page's Castellvi span and gap proxies, is flat (d under 0.2) and is not the same test.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Cite the anatomical and Castellvi-definition sources, and run the audit's two proposed mask tests (ilium contact, SI height against S1) before the book uses the SI anchor as established.

verdicts.topic: The audit's proposed sacral-boundary tests marked 'next' and the two-anchors design's 'may move' SI anchor
verdicts.quote_a: The sacral boundary has to come from something other than the label that already encodes it.
verdicts.quote_b: Lateral span and gap to the ala carry much of what Castellvi grades on, but they are not a graded read, and the flat effect sizes may reflect the proxy rather than the anatomy.
verdicts.explanation: The audit's 'next' tests are ilium contact with the L5 transverse process and sacroiliac height against the S1 endplate. The border page measured lateral span and gap to the ala, which is a sacral proxy, not ilium contact, and did not measure SI height. Both pages are undated. The texts do not show that the audit's tests were run.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Record whether the ilium-contact and SI-height tests were ever computed. If not, the audit's 'next' still stands, and the border page's flat proxies should be cited as related but not the same test.

verdicts.topic: Ribs on the wrong vertebra and misnumbered cases in CTSpinoPelvic1K v5
verdicts.quote_a: | on a different thoracic level — the defect | | 170 | | 109 | | −36% |
verdicts.quote_b: | Ribs on the wrong vertebra | | 109 | | 19 |
verdicts.explanation: Neither page is dated, but the border page's 'Before' column repeats exactly the audit's v5 'after' values (109 ribs, 16 misnumbered cases). Under 'Rib numbering, finished alongside this' it reports a later renumbering (lumbar-rib classes 74/75) that takes them to 19 and 2. It plainly follows and revises the audit's figures.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 19 ribs on the wrong vertebra and 2 misnumbered cases after the renumbering, with the audit's 170 to 109 as the earlier step. Check that the renumbering reached the released labels (v11) before treating 19 as the training labels' error count.

verdicts.topic: Prevalence of a sixth lumbar vertebra
verdicts.quote_a: A sixth lumbar vertebra occurs in roughly 2% of people, so the model is rewarded for never predicting one.
verdicts.quote_b: The expectation uses the acquisition plan's priors: any LSTV 9 % low (Hanhivaara 2020) to 18 % high (Nardo 2012); L6 3.2 % and four lumbar 1.6 % (Sun 2025), the two a mask count can call; T13 0.64 to 2.0 %.
verdicts.explanation: The design page states a population prevalence of about 2% with no source. The state-of-the-literature page (2026-10-08) uses a cited prior of 3.2% (Sun 2025) and reports CTSpinoPelvic1K's own read as 2.0% (Wilson 1.3 to 3.3%). The design page's figure matches the corpus read, not the cited population prior.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 3.2% (Sun 2025) as the population prior and 2.0% as CTSpinoPelvic1K's read, each with its source. Drop the unsourced 'roughly 2% of people' or relabel it as the corpus rate.

verdicts.topic: Number of L6 cases in CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_a: About 22 of 802 cases carry an L6 at all, roughly 2.7%.
verdicts.quote_b: CTSpinoPelvic1K L6: 18 by release label, 16 by the readers' own count, 29 persons in the registry.
verdicts.explanation: Both statements are present and disagree. The state-of-the-literature page (2026-10-08) reconciles the files it knows of into 18, 16 or 29 and puts seven disagreeing records out of every truth pool. Its list does not include 22, which matches no count in the 2026-10-08 pages (research-directions also gives Dataset813 18 L6). The decisions page is undated, and nothing says it was revised.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the 2026-10-08 reconciliation (18 by release label, 16 by readers, 7 records under re-read) and drop 'about 22' unless its source file is found. The seven re-reads named in research-directions settle the final count.

verdicts.topic: Number of four-lumbar (sacralised L5) cases in CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_a: | four lumbar | | 13 | | 3 | | 129 | | 145 | | trainable |
verdicts.quote_b: L6 18 by label and 16 by the readers; four-lumbar 9; no field reaches T1
verdicts.explanation: The overnight page (2026-09-16) tables 13 four-lumbar cases in the project's CTs. The research-directions page (2026-10-08, CTSpinoPelvic1K v11) gives 9, and the state-of-the-literature page agrees ('four lumbar 9'). That page also gives 13 as the expected number at the 1.6% prior, so the earlier 13 may be the expectation rather than a count, but nothing says so. The audit's 7 radiologist-read sacralizations are a 22-case subset and do not conflict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 9 (v11, read) as the count, and give 13 only as the prior-based expectation if that is its source. The overnight page's 13 should not be used as a training or test denominator.

verdicts.topic: Number of Castellvi-graded or non-normal LSTV labels in CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_a: 33 of 802 carry a non-normal label.
verdicts.quote_b: | Castellvi II–IV | | 31 | | 109 | | — | | 140 | | trainable |
verdicts.explanation: The three figures may be nested sets rather than rival counts. They are 33 non-normal labels (border page; research-directions also says 'Castellvi consensus on 33'), 31 Castellvi II-IV (overnight table), and 34 transitional-flag positives (overnight table, whose definition the overnight text does not give; the FluoroCap report describes 34 cases 'carrying an L6 or a Castellvi variant'). The texts do not give the membership of each set, so whether they conflict cannot be told.
verdicts.resolution_hint: One table of CTSpinoPelvic1K positives by definition (any non-normal label, Castellvi II-IV, L6, L6 or Castellvi) on the same release, with overlaps, would settle it. The book should name the definition beside each count.

verdicts.topic: VerSe sacralised and L6 counts used as the second CT source
verdicts.quote_a: L6 85 scans, T13 6, sacralised 13, Castellvi II 27, lumbar rib 12
verdicts.quote_b: | four lumbar | | 13 | | 3 | | 129 | | 145 | | trainable |
verdicts.explanation: L6 85 and T13 6 agree. Castellvi II 27 against II-IV 109 is a subset, not a conflict. 'Sacralised 13' against 'four lumbar 3' may be different definitions: a Castellvi sacralisation need not change the count. Research-directions itself records the VerSe L6 count as 85, 47, 50 or 87 across files, with no count from the raw masks. The overnight table also shows VerSe lumbar rib as '—' where research-directions gives 12. The texts do not settle whether any of these is the same quantity.
verdicts.resolution_hint: CT-3's planned raw-mask count of ids 25 and 28 against the Loeffler table settles the VerSe counts. Until it runs, the book should carry each VerSe figure with its definition and file.

verdicts.topic: Stump or hypoplastic twelfth ribs in CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_a: 67 cases fall below 0.30.
verdicts.quote_b: | stump / hypoplastic 12th rib | | — | | 90 | | — | | 90 | | trainable in count, at chance in result |
verdicts.explanation: The overnight table does not table zero for the project's CTs. It shows '—', and the same table writes '0' where it means zero (T13 vertebra, T13 rib) and '—' for VerSe lumbar rib, which research-directions later counts as 12. So '—' marks no labelled, usable count. The border page's 67 is a segmentation length-ratio measurement, not a label. The two count different things.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The book can carry both with their definitions: 67 CTSpinoPelvic1K cases below a rib-12/rib-11 length ratio of 0.30 (unread, and the audit warns that 57% of ribs are clipped by the field), and no labelled stump-rib cases in the project's CTs. Reading the 67 would make them usable positives.

verdicts.topic: Whether the twelfth rib in the field helps or hurts a variant flag
verdicts.quote_a: The tight lumbosacral junction view is the only field whose interval excludes chance at 0.656; the standard lumbar film sits at 0.509 and the wide field that shows the twelfth rib at 0.406, below chance.
verdicts.quote_b: It learns to count from the sacrum, and to count from the ribs, with ~800 cases of each.
verdicts.explanation: The overnight result is a whole-frame 2-D transitional flag on rendered fields. The design page is a 3-D per-voxel counting design on CT. Neither text speaks to the other's setting, so read in context they do not contradict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both, each with its scope. If the two-anchor idea is carried to fluoroscopy, cite the overnight render result as the measured 2-D framing outcome.

verdicts.topic: Which anchors the count runs against
verdicts.quote_a: For any target vertebra, the count above it plus the count below it must be 22.
verdicts.quote_b: | n_down | | how many it sits below the lowest rib-bearing vertebra | | every case |
verdicts.explanation: These are two different rules: C2 plus sacrum over a whole column (rule page, 2026-09-22), and sacrum plus lowest rib-bearing body (design page). Neither page claims the other is wrong, and each is internally consistent.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The book should state each rule's field requirement: the R + C = 22 rule needs C2 to the sacrum in view, and the two-anchor design needs the sacrum and the lowest rib in view. It should not present them as alternatives for the same field.

verdicts.topic: What happens on a column carrying both an extra and a missing segment
verdicts.quote_a: A column carrying both an extra and a missing vertebra sums to 22 and passes.
verdicts.quote_b: A lumbar rib and a sacralisation both reduce n_up + n_down by one.
verdicts.explanation: The statements concern different quantities. The rule page counts vertebrae between fixed ends (C2 and sacrum), where an extra and a missing body cancel. The design page counts segments between movable anchors, where a lumbar rib and a sacralisation each shorten the interval, so the sum drops by two, and the four-anchor signature separates them. Both are correct for their own rule.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both, each tied to its rule, and say that the double-variant blind spot belongs to fixed-end counting.

verdicts.topic: The T12-versus-L1 AUC 0.990 figure: its vertebra count and whether it is a single-vertebra result
verdicts.quote_a: On this corpus, T12 separates from L1 at AUC 0.990 and 97.3% accuracy over 1485 vertebrae, using shape alone with each patient's own size divided out.
verdicts.quote_b: The published 0.990 for T12 against L1 divides five of its eleven features by the patient's median over three or more levels, so it is not a single-vertebra classifier, and its dominant feature is the transverse-process span, which is coronal and invisible on a lateral.
verdicts.explanation: The design page offers 0.990 as the reason a per-vertebra thoracic-versus-lumbar head can repair the rib anchor on one vertebra. The research-directions page (2026-10-08) says the figure is not single-vertebra. It lists the anchor-ordinal design among the places searched for the ratio-only AUC, which is 'not on disk'. The vertebra counts also differ by one (1485 against 1,486 from 798 cases).
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the research-directions caveat with the 0.990 and give it as the within-patient ceiling. PAR-1, the one-hour ratio-only rerun, gives the single-vertebra number and fixes the vertebra count.

verdicts.topic: CTSpinoPelvic1K version state: v5 as a local tree never pushed
verdicts.quote_a: v5 exists as a local tree on the grid at data/v5_final. Nothing has been pushed to a HuggingFace branch.
verdicts.quote_b: Rebuild the lateral and AP projected-landmark bank from the v11 tree, never the v10 Hugging Face mirror.
verdicts.explanation: The audit's statement of state is about v5. The research-directions page (2026-10-08) names a v11 label tree on the grid and a v10 Hugging Face mirror, so the dataset has moved six versions on and a mirror has been pushed. The audit's sentence is a past state. Its counts, and the border page's (also data/v5_final), are on a superseded label generation.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Mark every count from the audit and border pages as v5. The book should give the current state as v11 on the grid with a v10 public mirror, and recompute any count it carries forward on v11.

verdicts.topic: The two-anchors design's five experimental arms
verdicts.quote_a: Run arms 1 and 2 as a matched pair on the same folds. The delta between them is the result.
verdicts.quote_b: | CT-7, the anchor-ordinal design | do two dense ordinal fields, from the sacrum and from the lowest rib-bearing body, plus a per-body type, flag the variant as a consistency violation | arms 1 and 2 as a matched pair on the same folds |
verdicts.explanation: The design page is a plan and never claims the arms ran. The 2026-10-08 page carries the same first experiment forward as CT-7, ranked within row 14. Its 'Nothing ran on the grid' refers to how that document was written, not to CT-7. The texts agree that the arms are planned and unrun.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The book can carry the design as current, with the note that as of 2026-10-08 it is CT-7, unrun, and ranked behind the visibility and truth work.

verdicts.topic: 'Counts quoted are measured on the released labels' of CTSpinoPelvic1K
verdicts.quote_a: Counts quoted are measured on the released labels.
verdicts.quote_b: CTSpinoPelvic1K L6: 18 by release label, 16 by the readers' own count, 29 persons in the registry. Seven disagreeing records are out of every truth pool until re-read.
verdicts.explanation: The design page does not name which release it measured. The later page puts seven L6 records under re-read but does not revise the design page's counts (sixteen lumbar ribs, the foramina distribution by normal label). Whether those counts change cannot be told from the texts.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Name the release behind the design page's counts. After the seven re-reads, recompute the normal-labelled foramina table and the lumbar-rib count on v11.

verdicts.topic: Seven CTSpinoPelvic1K cases that 'need a person' and the v5 spine reviews not finalized
verdicts.quote_a: 0008 — labelled SACRALIZATION , the only reader disagreement of the fourteen, and shifted +1 during this pass.
verdicts.quote_b: Both review cohorts were complete and both on the v4 label scheme — 169/169 rib cases and 107/113 spine cases finalized, zero rejects.
verdicts.explanation: Both statements are present and both are v5-era. No text in the cluster says whether the seven open cases or the six unfinalized spine reviews were resolved before v11. The research-directions page's 'seven CTSpinoPelvic1K re-reads' concern L6 records, which the text does not tie to these seven.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Check the v11 review ledger for cases 0008, 0389, 0720, 0344, 0179, 0412 and 1153 and the six outstanding spine reviews, and record their state. Until then the book should list them as open as of v5.

verdicts.topic: The LSTV verification bench of 585 transitional figures
verdicts.quote_a: 0 reviewed of 0 · usable human X-ray/fluoro: 0 · with a transitional finding: 0
verdicts.quote_b: | FluoroCap | 29,500 panels | dropped by directive; the 200-panel test set does not exist | annotate about 200 or write it off |
verdicts.explanation: The bench's '0 reviewed of 0' is a static placeholder: the page's script fills the total from the rows (bench_data.js holds 585 entries) and the reviewed count from a live store. So the exported text says nothing about how many figures were marked. The research-directions row concerns a 200-panel FluoroCap test set, not this transitional bench. Whether any of the 585 were reviewed is not in the records.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Read the bench's store, or record its verdict count, to settle whether any of the 585 figures were marked. The book should not say the bench is empty on the strength of the static text.

verdicts.topic: Existence of a real intraoperative fluoroscopy set with level labels
verdicts.quote_a: The comparator, LevelCheck, needs the patient's preoperative CT (or MRI) and 3D–2D registration; it placed labels in the correct level on all 398 radiographs it was run on (after excluding 21 poor-quality films), was judged helpful in 42.2% and most helpful in the thoracic spine (77.7%) versus 33.5% lumbar, but has never demonstrated a reduction in wrong-level error, and no surviving claim gives wrong-level incidence, mechanism, or a public intraoperative fluoroscopy dataset with level labels.
verdicts.quote_b: You hold the large open vertebra-labelled spine CT releases the prior research names, the CT fetched to find transitional spines, 9,108 level-labelled real plain films, and exactly one real intraoperative human set with a volume.
verdicts.explanation: The two agree once read in context. The state-of-the-literature page says C-ArmLSpine's levels come from 'two automatic labellers' run by the programme, with 'no human-read levels', so it is not a public intraoperative dataset with level labels. The feasibility page's literature verdict (2026-09-15) still holds.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The book can carry both: no public intraoperative set with released level labels, and one held human intraoperative set (C-ArmLSpine) whose levels are automatic and unread.

verdicts.topic: Whether registration-free single-frame level naming on real radiographs has a measured per-level accuracy
verdicts.quote_a: Realistic promise for a registration-free single-frame alert: a binary LSTV / TLTV / atypical-count flag with modest specificity that triggers a whole-spine count or preoperative-CT check, with explicit abstention when the sacrum, odontoid or twelfth rib is outside the field or when a numerical variant (T13, L6, lumbarised S1) is suspected; not a Castellvi type and not an authoritative level name at the lumbosacral junction.
verdicts.quote_b: In the isolated-stack state on real film, exact naming was 97.2% [96.9, 97.4] on ordinary spines (n = 14,492) and 87.2% [84.3, 89.7] on anomalous spines (n = 572); pseudolabel training lowered the anomalous figure to 66.8% [62.9, 70.4].
verdicts.explanation: The feasibility page (2026-09-15) summarises what the verified literature establishes. The naming page (2026-09-17) reports the programme's own unpublished measurement, so the two are compatible. The 'feasibility report' the naming page argues against uses field-of-view states A to C and a Wigh band, which this artifact does not contain, so it is not shown to be this page. On the lumbosacral point they agree: the naming page's later v6 figure is 49.9% on anomalous interior windows, 'a coin toss', and it says 'That is the one place the report's argument holds'.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the feasibility page as the literature state on 2026-09-15 and the naming page as the programme's own result. Use the v6 numbers (81.3% label-defined State C, 49.9% anomalous interior) over the 20-film 87.2%.

verdicts.topic: Real panels labelled T13 or L6 in the FluoroCap corpus
verdicts.quote_a: The corpus itself still has no real panel labelled T13 or L6; the pathology search (158,955 articles, 1,961 level-bearing figures matched so far, still reading) is the route to them.
verdicts.quote_b: 20,700 panels decoded and 11,377 carrying a level, against 5,789 and 4,614 yesterday morning.
verdicts.explanation: The FluoroCap report (15 September, 08:30) says no real panel carries a T13 or L6 label. The next overnight page (dated 2026-09-16) revises the corpus counts against 'yesterday morning'. Its level table lists L6 on 338 panels (145 caption-named, 193 caption-free) and T13 on 254, after the decoder was changed to allow T13 and L6. The '0 of 16' T13 result is model accuracy on renders, a separate quantity.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the later counts, labelled as caption-named or decoder-derived and not human-verified, and note that FluoroCap was later dropped from training (research-directions, 2026-10-08).

verdicts.topic: Population prevalence of lumbosacral transitional vertebrae
verdicts.quote_a: 3,461 normal / 15 lumbarization / 130 sacralization — 4.0% prevalence, which is the population rate rather than a referral-enriched one.
verdicts.quote_b: The target is therefore the count-changing types II to IV, 9 to 11 % of CTs.
verdicts.explanation: The board (2026-09-11), echoed by the decisions page, calls BUU's 4.0% the population rate. The research-directions page (2026-10-08) puts count-changing types alone at 9 to 11% of CTs, and the state-of-the-literature page cites any LSTV at 9% (Hanhivaara 2020) to 18% (Nardo 2012). The naming page says BUU's negatives are 'contaminated by construction', because a Castellvi I-IV segment on a five-lumbar spine is not recorded.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the cited priors as the population rate, and describe BUU's 4.0% as the dataset's recorded four- and six-lumbar rate, a floor rather than a prevalence. Drop the board's 'population rate' reading.

verdicts.topic: BUU-LSPINE anomalous study counts
verdicts.quote_a: 3,461 normal / 15 lumbarization / 130 sacralization — 4.0% prevalence, which is the population rate rather than a referral-enriched one.
verdicts.quote_b: For real radiographs, BUU-LSPINE ships its authors' own per-study reading of four-lumbar (129) or six-lumbar (15) anatomy, four corner keypoints per body, S1 end-plate corners on laterals, and a pixel spacing of 0.175 mm.
verdicts.explanation: 130 sacralizations against 129 four-lumbar studies is a real difference in the texts. The board's three counts sum to 3,606, more than BUU's 3,600 studies, and the board says they come from the class field on lateral films. So it likely counts lateral films, including a few extra files (research-directions mentions 3,603 laterals), not studies. The naming page (2026-09-17) counts per study: '15 promoted, 129 flagged'.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the per-study figures 129 and 15 (144 of 3,600). Note that the board's 130 and its 3,606 total are lateral-film counts. Checking which study holds the extra sacralization file settles the one-case difference.

verdicts.topic: BUU LSTV truth marked 'unused'
verdicts.quote_a: BUU ships LSTV ground truth nobody was reading
verdicts.quote_b: v6 moves all 144 to the test partition (a 144-film anomalous test set instead of 20), duplicates anomalous CT renders ×4 in training, and changes nothing else—so the ordinary column is a control rather than a moving target.
verdicts.explanation: On 2026-09-11 the board tagged BUU's LSTV truth 'unused' (the candidate's wording 'BUU ships unused LSTV truth (3,461 / 15 / 130, 4.0%) and slip grades' is not in the board's text, whose heading is the line quoted). By 2026-09-17 the naming page uses those reads to define the anomalous real-film stratum and moves all 144 studies to test. The later page plainly overtakes the board's status.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the later state: BUU's four- and six-lumbar reads are the real-film anomalous test partition, barred from training, and are no longer a free training source.

verdicts.topic: Castellvi type I is about two thirds (68%) of all lumbosacral transitional anatomy
verdicts.quote_a: It is about two thirds of all transitional anatomy, it is not separable in any source we hold, and it therefore sits inside every negative set we train and measure against.
verdicts.quote_b: Castellvi type I is a coronal transverse-process height of 19 mm or more, 68 % of all LSTV, and unrecoverable from a lateral film by construction.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages state the share with no citation at the statement. The research-directions page repeats it as a gate ('type I near 68 % of calls') with no source there either. The target choice (types II to IV) and the claim that every negative set is contaminated rest on it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Find and cite the source of the 68% figure, perhaps among the priors the state-of-the-literature page names, before the book states it. Otherwise mark it as unsourced.

verdicts.topic: The VerSe rare-class precedent: how many L6 training cases make L6 learnable
verdicts.quote_a: The published precedent on rare classes is sobering and specific: in VerSe, with two L6 training cases no algorithm out of about ten identified an L6; with fifteen, most identified some.
verdicts.quote_b: 377 L6 people are expected against the 85 L6 scans in VerSe'20, where 28 in training sufficed to make L6 learnable.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages state the precedent with no reference at the statement. They also give different thresholds (fifteen against 28), which may be different challenge phases or cases against scans, and neither says which. Research-directions repeats the 28 ('the 28 L6 training scans that sufficed in VerSe'20') without a reference.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Cite the VerSe challenge report for the L6 training counts per phase and the outcome per phase, and carry one threshold with its unit. That source settles the 15 against 28 difference.

verdicts.topic: The 1.6% prevalence figure: lumbar rib or four lumbar vertebrae
verdicts.quote_a: prevalence windows: thirteen rib-bearing 0.37 to 0.88 %, lumbar rib 1.6 %
verdicts.quote_b: The expectation uses the acquisition plan's priors: any LSTV 9 % low (Hanhivaara 2020) to 18 % high (Nardo 2012); L6 3.2 % and four lumbar 1.6 % (Sun 2025), the two a mask count can call; T13 0.64 to 2.0 %.
verdicts.explanation: The two pages give 1.6% for two different variants: a lumbar rib on one, four lumbar vertebrae (Sun 2025) on the other. Two variants can share a rate, and the research-directions cell gives no source, so the texts do not show whether this is a coincidence or a transcription error.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Trace the source of CT-8's lumbar-rib 1.6%. If it is Sun 2025's four-lumbar prior, correct it. If it has its own source, cite it.

verdicts.topic: Number of L6 persons available to the programme
verdicts.quote_a: The model has never seen a photograph of a six-lumbar spine. All 168 are CT renders.
verdicts.quote_b: 86 of the 110 L6 persons are VerSe's own, so beyond VerSe the holding adds 24.
verdicts.explanation: The figures have different scopes: 168 distinct L6 patients across the 2-D training renders (2026-09-17), 110 L6 persons in the CT-labelling comparison row, and 146 L6 in the acquisition registry excluding VerSe (2026-10-08). The texts do not say which label pools each draws on, or whether 168 counts screen-flagged acquisition CTs that the later page treats as unverified. They neither reconcile nor clearly contradict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: One person-level L6 table by pool (VerSe, CTSpinoPelvic1K, TotalSegmentator, registry, read or unread) with the render banks' membership would settle it. The book should name the pool beside each figure.

verdicts.topic: Number of CTSpinoPelvic1K cases labelled normal
verdicts.quote_a: Counting foramina per side across 802 records gives, for cases labelled normal : 2 in 211 cases, 3 in 324, 4 in 163, 5 in 49.
verdicts.quote_b: 33 of 802 carry a non-normal label.
verdicts.explanation: The foramina list gives only the bins 2 to 5 and never claims to cover every normal-labelled case. The detector returns other values (the border page reports 7 on one side of one sacrum), and truncated sacra may return 0 or 1. So 747 in the listed bins against 769 normal labels is not a contradiction.
verdicts.resolution_hint: If the book carries the foramina table, add the remaining bins (0, 1, 6 or more, undetermined) so it sums to the normal-labelled total on the stated release.

verdicts.topic: BUU LSTV truth and the published radiograph LSTV state of the art
verdicts.quote_a: Published SOTA on radiographs is AUC 0.84, binary, single centre, at 62.3% prevalence.
verdicts.quote_b: Published SOTA is AUC 0.84, binary, single centre, at 62.3% prevalence.
verdicts.explanation: The two pages carry the same sentence with the same BUU counts and the same 'population prevalence' reading, and neither names the study. The feasibility page cites it (Kwak, Ro, Kang, J Clin Med 2025, 3,116 films, 313-film test set), and research-directions gives Kwak 2025 at a 62% positive rate. The two copies are one unsourced claim, not two confirmations.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the claim once, cited to Kwak 2025 as the feasibility page gives it, and drop the 'population prevalence' reading of BUU's 4.0% (see the prevalence candidate).

verdicts.topic: The programme's headline 2-D naming figures and the encoder leak
verdicts.quote_a: 97.4 % of bodies named on a whole lateral frame and 74.8 % with one body in view; the count alone names 97.0 % of anchored bodies and the coupling adds 1.2 points
verdicts.quote_b: On ordinary spines the 2-D system is at ceiling on plain film and near ceiling on the one real C-arm: it names 97.4 % of bodies on a whole lateral frame and 74.8 % with one body in view.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 2026-10-08 and come from the same account. They share the naming figures and the leak statement word for word or nearly so (handoff: '92 of 97 transitional validation and test persons sit in the current encoder's training lineage'; research-directions: '92 of 97 transitional validation and test persons sit in the v8 and v9 training splits'). They are one source, not two.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Cite the figures once, to the underlying HANDOFF files in spinesurg-ct-nnunet that both pages name, and do not count the two pages as independent confirmation.

verdicts.topic: The COBRA one-labeller screen precision and the transitional power targets
verdicts.quote_a: The same labeller matched reader truth on 10 of 24 L6 and 0 of 52 T13 in CTSpinoPelvic1K, so it is not trusted.
verdicts.quote_b: registry L6 146 and T13 14; the one-labeller COBRA screen is not trusted (precision 10 of 24 on L6, 0 of 52 on T13)
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 2026-10-08, and they carry the same precision figures and the same power targets (35 error-free at-risk persons, 22 carriers, 19 for paper 2's H1, planning values of 95 to 99% unsupported). This is one audit restated, not two.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Cite once, to HANDOFF/LITERATURE_STATE.md in spinesurg-ct-nnunet as the state-of-the-literature page names it.

verdicts.topic: The decisions page's open question on L6 Dice 0.00 and the running fold count
verdicts.quote_a: Counting how the rare classes fall across the five folds is running now. It decides whether consolidating folds helps, or whether the fix has to be class-aware patch sampling.
verdicts.quote_b: | L6 as a voxel class, 18 cases duplicated twelvefold | Dice 0.000 every epoch | measured |
verdicts.explanation: The decisions page is undated, but its content (fold 4 alone on an H200 from epoch 50, the IRB purge done) follows the 2026-09-11 board. It leaves the L6 question 'investigating'. The 2026-10-08 page records oversampling by duplication as measured and failed, and moves the question to CT-6 (the L6 learnability curve) and CT-7 (the anchor-ordinal design). Class-aware patch sampling as such is not recorded as tried.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the 2026-10-08 state: twelvefold duplication gave Dice 0.000, and CT-6 and CT-7 are the open routes. Keep 'class-aware patch sampling not yet tried' as a separate, explicit open item rather than the decisions page's 'investigating'.
